learningSummary: A business arranging commercial cleaning can fall within California’s janitorial registration program even if franchisees or contractors perform the work. The customer receiving cleaning has a different role from either provider.

sections.heading: Does your company provide or arrange the cleaning?
paragraphs: The Labor Commissioner’s explanation covers an entity employing a covered worker or engaging through contracts, subcontracts or franchise arrangements for covered janitorial services. Covered workers can include employees, independent contractors and franchisees predominantly working as janitors. The FAQ includes commercial providers without employees.

For example, if your U.S. company signs an office-cleaning contract and a franchisee performs it, the office is the recipient; the company and franchisee each need their own provider analysis. The restaurant-customer example does not automatically exempt them.

The FAQ excludes a provider cleaning only residential dwellings and gives a separate interpretation for public entities; the reviewed rule applies to private entities. These are role-and-work distinctions, not a general intermediary exemption.

sections.heading: Registration costs $500 and lasts one year
paragraphs: The program states a $500 nonrefundable initial fee and $500 annual renewal fee. Renew by the month and day of original issuance, not an application-drafting date.

Section 13810 asks for entity, customer and contractor/franchisee information. Workers’ compensation evidence is conditional on employing one or more employees; the broader covered-worker definition does not make every contractor or franchisee an employee.

sections.heading: Keep worker records and check contracting providers
paragraphs: Keep the required employee and other covered-worker records, including work periods and compensation, for three years. When entering, extending, renewing or modifying a janitorial contract, check the counterparty’s registration as the cited requirements direct.

practicalOutput: Identify each company that arranges or performs the cleaning, then check its registration position before the first job or contract change.
limitations: This is the named janitorial registration program. Worker classification, wages, training and other operating permissions use separate requirements.
editNote: Owner question: Does registration cover the company arranging cleaning as well as the franchisee doing it? Subtractive decision: Cut “Follow the Singapore example one legal entity at a time” and trim “Prepare the provider schedule before the first job” to the required registration, renewal and record duties. Replace “Assign the application documents” with the actual action. Final focus: Lead with who supplies or arranges commercial cleaning, then explain the recipient and residential-only exceptions; give the filing cost and renewal date once.
conditionsRetained: Contract/subcontract/franchise arrangements and nonemployee covered workers; commercial provider without employees.
$500 nonrefundable initial/$500 annual; one year; original issue anniversary.
Workers’ compensation evidence only if one or more employees.
Three-year covered-worker records and stated contract-event registration checks.

learningSummary: California’s janitorial training rules cover relevant workers and supervisors, potentially including contractors and franchisees. A past video or a training provider’s certificate must meet this program’s actual course and proof requirements.

sections.heading: Who needs training, and by when?
paragraphs: The program covers nonsupervisory covered workers and their supervisors; follow the actual janitorial roles rather than payroll alone. Identify the janitorial employer responsible.

Section 13821 requires at least two hours at least once every two years and training within six months after assuming a new covered position. Split segments must each last at least one hour. A cleaner promoted to supervisor therefore raises a new-position deadline and the supervisor training route.

A defined successor employer may carry forward a retained worker’s documented last-training date only if the workforce-retention, seniority, wage and policy conditions are satisfied. Taking over a customer contract alone is insufficient.

sections.heading: Use the right trainer, format and language
paragraphs: The Department of Industrial Relations (DIR) says in-person compliance must begin following publication of the qualified-organization list in January 2024. It distinguishes qualified peer trainers for nonsupervisory workers from qualified supervisor trainers.

Required content is developed through the Labor Occupational Health Program under DIR’s direction. Training must match participants’ language and literacy. A general online orientation or English-only certificate does not establish those requirements.

sections.heading: The employer remains responsible for proof
paragraphs: Even if another entity supplies training, the employer must keep the required records for at least three years and make them available to the Labor Commissioner.
bullets: Keep participant and role details, position-start and training dates, printed names and signatures at the start and completion, certificates, content and provider identity.
Retain signed DLSE 800 compliance and the required certification about payment of the qualified organization.
Provide the trainee’s materials and attendance or completion certificate when requested.

practicalOutput: Check each person’s role-start and last-training dates, then arrange the appropriate course and required proof.
limitations: Limited to this janitorial training program. Registration, wages, classification and other training laws remain separate.
editNote: Owner question: What training does a newly promoted cleaning supervisor need, and by when? Subtractive decision: Remove “Answer the promoted-cleaner question with the right record”; combine “The employer keeps the records” with the required-record bullets rather than repeating a “person-by-person training register” in the ending. Final focus: Help the owner decide whether the existing course evidence is sufficient or a suitable supervisor course must be arranged; distinguish the legal course conditions from an optional spreadsheet.
conditionsRetained: Two hours/two years; six months new position; each segment at least one hour.
Qualified peer versus supervisor trainers; January2024 in-person list trigger; required content, language/literacy.
Employer proof responsibility despite outsourced training; at least3years; signatures, DLSE800, payment certification, trainee access.

learningSummary: For the stated 2026 executive-exemption illustration, a $120,000 employment budget does not make a $65,000 base salary sufficient. Salary, actual duties and the applicable worksite and industry rules are different tests.

sections.heading: Start with the actual worksite and industry
paragraphs: The MW-2026 order sets California’s general minimum at $16.90 per hour from January 1, 2026, subject to its application provisions. Fast-food and healthcare requirements are separate, and local rates may be higher. A headquarters address does not determine every customer-site rate.

sections.heading: A manager title does not establish the executive exemption
paragraphs: The Labor Commissioner’s guidance combines management of the enterprise or recognized unit; regular direction of two or more employees; hiring/firing authority or recommendations given particular weight; discretion and independent judgment; primarily exempt duties; and the required salary.

A launch manager spending substantial time cleaning, delivering services or following prescribed instructions still needs assessment against those actual duties. Raising pay alone does not settle the test.

sections.heading: Separate guaranteed salary from employer cost
paragraphs: The executive entry describes monthly salary of at least twice the state minimum for full-time employment, using a 40-hour week. At the general 2026 rate, the annualized illustration is $16.90 × 40 × 52 × 2 = $70,304.

In the fictional $120,000 budget, only $65,000 is promised as base salary; the rest covers employer costs and launch support. The total exceeds $70,304, but the base salary does not meet that illustrated component. Taxes, benefits, insurance, recruitment and equipment are not automatically guaranteed salary.
Even a sufficient guaranteed salary leaves the duties, actual wage order and any overtime questions. This illustration is not the test for every industry or another exemption.

practicalOutput: Price the job using its actual worksite, duties and guaranteed pay, then calculate total employer cost separately.
limitations: This is a 2026 general-rate and executive-exemption illustration, not an actual classification or a 2027 rate. Other exemptions and industry wage orders require their own tests.
editNote: Owner question: Can I treat a $65,000 manager as overtime-exempt because the full employment budget is $120,000? Subtractive decision: Cut “Self-check: what does the $120,000 budget prove?” and shorten “Prepare the hiring and pricing records”; keep the calculation with the example rather than restating it in three places. Final focus: Answer the budget question first: total employer cost is not guaranteed salary, and meeting the salary component still leaves the duties and applicable wage-order tests.
conditionsRetained: All cumulative executive conditions; monthly salary rule40hr; annualized$70304 notallindustrytest.

learningSummary: Before replacing an Idaho equipment dealer or appointing another nearby, identify the covered equipment relationship and the actual action. The ordinary exit, weak-sales and new-dealer rules are different.

sections.heading: Check the dealer definition and combined exclusion
paragraphs: Chapter 28-24 can cover continuing oral/written and express/implied rights to sell, distribute or service a supplier’s equipment. The dealer must meet the Idaho primarily retail sale and/or service definition. Specified outdoor-power, industrial and construction equipment can qualify; using a machine for cleaning alone does not.

The industrial/construction-dealer exclusion requires all stated conditions: the primary-business condition, at least 75% of total new-product inventory bought from one supplier, and annual average sales exceeding $20 million with that supplier over the preceding three years in the responsible territory. The product category alone is insufficient.

sections.heading: Ordinary notice and cure have different exceptions
paragraphs: Section 28-24-104 requires written notice stating good-cause reasons. The ordinary process gives at least 90 days’ advance notice and 90 days to cure, with protection against early agreement expiry in the specified circumstances.

Notice exceptions refer to subsection (2)(a)–(e), while cure exceptions refer to (a)–(d). An exception to one period does not automatically remove the other. The ground, evidence and comparable dealer requirements matter.

sections.heading: Weak sales are not the same as a nearby appointment
paragraphs: For market-penetration action, section 104(3) has a separate one-year notice and reasonable supplier-assistance stage, followed by the specified 180-day notice if its conditions remain. A generic poor-sales letter does not complete it.

Section 104A separately requires notice to identified existing dealers for a new or relocated dealership. Assigned areas matter; the 75-mile alternative applies where no area is assigned. That notice does not create exclusivity.
Section 103 also addresses coerced amendments, substantial-renovation conditions, product-line changes and other supplier conduct.

practicalOutput: Choose the actual proposed action only after testing coverage, then apply its own notice, correction or assistance conditions.
limitations: Limited to the named Chapter 28-24 provisions. General franchise-sales, other product-line, contract and dispute rules are not resolved.
editNote: Owner question: Can I replace a weak-selling equipment dealer or appoint another nearby? Subtractive decision: Use the substantive rows in “Do not replace a combined test with one convenient fact” instead of the matching prose, rather than both. Cut the generic “Keep the decision records together” recap and narrow the example to replacement versus nearby appointment. Final focus: Let the owner choose the proposed action—replacement for performance or a nearby appointment—after the product/dealer coverage gate; show only the relevant process next.

learningSummary: A Colorado supplier’s demand for new premises at renewal has different conditions from replacing a dealer for weak sales. First confirm that the machines and retail business fall within Article 38.

sections.heading: Which equipment and agreements are covered?
paragraphs: The Farm Equipment Fair Dealership Act includes machines designed or adapted and used for the stated agricultural, horticultural, floricultural (flower-growing), light-industrial, utility and outdoor-power purposes. It excludes earthmoving/heavy construction, mining and forestry equipment. The dealer must be primarily engaged in retail equipment sales.

Section 35-38-102 includes oral or written, fixed- or indefinite-term dealer agreements setting purchase/sale rights and obligations. Section 110 has agreement-date and change conditions; it voids foreign-law or foreign-venue clauses only with respect to an otherwise enforceable claim under the article.

sections.heading: Do not assume every default gets the same 180 days
paragraphs: Covered termination, nonrenewal and substantial competitive changes require cause. Section 104’s 180-day written notice/cure process expressly excepts the first ten grounds in subsection (2)(b)(I)–(X), including specified agreement, payment and other failures.

Where the process applies, notice must give reasons and the 180-day cure information. The specified period is protected against early expiry or competitive change without written consent. Actual grounds and similarly situated dealer treatment must be examined.

sections.heading: A premises demand needs its own advance notice
paragraphs: Section 103(1)(d) restricts substantial renovation or new/additional premises as a condition of renewal or extension. It requires at least one year’s written notice, all grounds and a reasonable completion period after that year.

Thus an outdoor-power supplier demanding a showroom and threatening replacement for weak sales raises two separate rules. A renewal clause alone does not establish the premises conditions; a missed target alone does not establish cause or the applicable exception.

practicalOutput: Identify the machines and separate any premises demand from the proposed exit before committing to a deadline or site expenditure.
limitations: Limited to Article 38’s named scope and relationship provisions. Inventory recovery and disputes remain separate; exclusion here does not show there are no rights under another law.
editNote: Owner question: Can a supplier demand a new showroom at renewal or replace a dealer for weak sales? Subtractive decision: Delete “The showroom demand and replacement threat need different records”; trim the “Prepare a product-and-action file” recap and say directly that the showroom demand has different conditions from ending the dealership. Final focus: Compare the two supplier demands directly: what must be established before requiring new premises, and which cause/notice conditions govern replacement.

learningSummary: In Minnesota, ending a franchise early, refusing renewal and deciding whether to approve its buyer are different actions. The purpose of taking over an operator’s premises also matters; changing the label on a notice does not settle the rule.

sections.heading: Identify the covered relationship and intended action
paragraphs: Start with the franchise definition in section 80C.01. Some franchise categories specifically recognised by the Commissioner receive different treatment under section 80C.14 subdivisions 1–2; check that coverage before applying the termination and nonrenewal rules below. Registration expiry is separate from the operator agreement’s expiry.

For example, if a brand wants the premises for its own operation when a weak-performing operator’s term ends, the actual purpose matters. The nonrenewal provision prohibits refusal for that conversion purpose.

sections.heading: Use the branch for the actual decision
paragraphs: The conditions below do not establish cause, value or an entitlement to approve or reject any actual action. “Cure” means correcting the stated failure. A going concern is the business valued as a continuing operation, rather than only its separate assets or initial fee.

rows: Good cause; 90-day written notice stating all reasons and 60 days from receipt to correct, subject to separate immediate-effect exceptions. Examine material/reasonable obligations and actual correction.

Specified abandonment, business-related conviction and prescribed uncured goodwill-default branch have separate conditions. The goodwill branch itself requires the prescribed prior cure notice; a listed cause is not automatically an immediate-notice exception.

Separate good-cause/failure-to-correct branches, or at least 180 days’ advance notice plus the stated opportunity to operate long enough to recover fair market value as a going concern, measured from failure to renew. This is not an automatic cash refund, compensation payment or return of the initial fee.

Consent may not be unreasonably withheld where the replacement meets the franchisor’s present qualifications and standards. Compare the actual buyer and reasons with those current standards; not every buyer must be approved.

practicalOutput: Identify whether you propose early termination, nonrenewal or a transfer decision before selecting a notice period or assessing money consequences.
limitations: Limited to the stated franchise/classification scope of section 80C.14. Going-concern valuation, complete Commissioner rules, sector, bankruptcy and judicial analysis are not supplied.
editNote: Owner question: Can I end this operator’s agreement, refuse renewal or reject its buyer? Subtractive decision: Use “Select the actual relationship decision before selecting days” as the primary comparison, retaining its legal conditions; cut “Prepare one decision file for the actual action” and the example’s closing “exercise produces questions and a factual record”. Final focus: Start with the actual intended action and purpose. Explain the applicable branch directly, with the takeover example showing why a nonrenewal label does not avoid the conversion prohibition.
conditionsRetained: Goodcause90reasons60fromreceipt; distinct immediate grounds and goodwillpriorcure.

learningSummary: Ending a Connecticut franchise and recovering premises leased to its operator can require different procedures. The notice period depends on the reason; a standard 60-day email does not complete every exit.

sections.heading: The state relationship test is separate
paragraphs: Section 42-133e describes oral/written marketing-plan and brand arrangements and specified distribution relationships without stating a franchise-fee element. The merchandising-concession qualification and section 42-133h’s agreement-date and Connecticut place-of-business conditions also matter.
A federal fee result or business-opportunity trademark exclusion does not decide this relationship-law coverage.

sections.heading: Choose notice from the actual ground
paragraphs: Section 42-133f generally requires good cause, including substantial refusal or failure to meet a material and reasonable agreement obligation. These advance-notice branches do not create a universal 60-day right to cure.

rows: Ordinary covered termination, cancellation or nonrenewal
At least 60 days’ written notice stating cause.
Six months’ notice; not every nonrenewal falls within this branch.
Specified serious conviction directly related to the franchise business
Different provision effective on delivery and written receipt; not any conviction or ordinary email.

sections.heading: A connected lease and compensation need separate attention
paragraphs: Where the franchisor leases premises under a lease ending with the franchise and seeks to end it, section 42-133f(b) requires service by a state marshal or a person meeting the “indifferent person” requirement, specified lease/rights wording, and reproduction and attachment of the two statutory sections. Section 42-133g separately addresses continued occupation, temporary injunctions and court filings for possession.

For the stated agreements, section 42-133f also addresses minimum three-year initial and successive terms and conditional termination compensation for inventory, supplies, equipment and furnishings obtained from the franchisor or approved sources. Personalized items without value to the franchisor are excluded. The section addresses void waivers; notice does not itself value assets or establish possession or damages.

practicalOutput: Identify the actual exit ground and whether you are also ending a connected lease before choosing notice, service and possession steps.
limitations: The official base-code mirror matches the 2025 edition; histories and the available 2026 supplement index were examined, but later session laws and special industries were not fully certified.
Petroleum, motor-vehicle and business-opportunity laws have separate definitions.
editNote: Owner question: If I own the operator’s workshop, can I end the franchise and recover the premises with one notice? Subtractive decision: Lead with the answer from “A connected lease requires a different delivery and court file”; combine the repeated notice prose and “Choose the reason-dependent notice, then check the lease layer” into one comparison. Remove the opening talk of an “exit file”. Final focus: Explain the two linked decisions: ending a covered franchise and seeking possession under its connected lease. Show which notices and court questions differ without treating the record folder as the result.

learningSummary: Florida section 817.416 addresses intentional misrepresentations about success, required investment and market capacity for relationships within its own definition. An exemption notice does not validate those claims.

sections.heading: First check this statute’s definition
paragraphs: The reviewed 2026 text requires its specified commercial relationship, granted offering/selling/distribution rights, an independent business within a distribution system, and substantial reliance on the franchisor for basic goods supply. It can include express/implied and oral/written arrangements.

Goods can include articles used or consumed in an approved service. Core chemical or equipment supply may therefore matter for a cleaning network; using a brand alone does not establish a pure advisory business is covered. Neither the federal franchise test nor section 559.802 notice replaces this definition.

sections.heading: Check what you say about success, costs and capacity
paragraphs: For a covered sale or establishment, section 817.416(2)(a) addresses intentional misrepresentation of prospects or chances of success, known required total investment, and efforts to establish more operators than the market or market area can reasonably sustain.

For example, two territories promoted as highly profitable might depend on the same customers. Compare the actual investment—including relevant omissions—and market information with what you say. Preserve the statement, audience, timing and what was known. That comparison is practical preparation, not authorization to make a financial performance representation.

sections.heading: A remedy requires the civil showing
paragraphs: Under section 817.416(3), a person showing a violation in civil court may receive judgment for all money invested. The court may award reasonable attorney fees and shall award reasonable costs on that showing. Fees are not automatic, and a possible judgment is not guaranteed recovery.
This is not a general cancellation right or a rule deciding ordinary termination, good cause or contract-performance disputes.

practicalOutput: Before using a profitability, investment or territory-capacity claim, check the actual relationship and the facts and omissions behind that statement.
limitations: Definition, intent and the civil-court showing remain factual conditions. This does not complete federal earnings-claim, consumer-protection or other industry rules.
editNote: Owner question: What can go wrong when I promise profitable territories and quote opening costs? Subtractive decision: Delete “Prepare a claims register” and merge “Match each claim to the fact that needs support” with the chemical-supply example. Cut “The aim is to let the business and reviewer see” while retaining what was said and known. Final focus: Answer which statements the statute targets, for which supply-dependent relationships, then use one short example to show an omitted investment amount or overlapping territories.

learningSummary: A covered Minnesota offer or sale needs effective registration unless exempt. Use the Commissioner’s actual order for the registration period, and treat buyer delivery and any restriction on initial fees as separate requirements.

sections.heading: An application is not effective registration
paragraphs: Section 80C.01 subdivision 4 includes a route involving brand rights, a shared commercial interest (community of interest), and a direct or indirect fee and other branches for fuel, specified business-opportunity promises and certain security-system payments. Area franchises, fee definitions/exclusions and wholesale or fair-market-value treatment need their own conditions; the federal control-or-assistance test is not a substitute.

Under sections 80C.02–.03, covered offers/sales require effective registration unless the franchise or transaction is exempt. The Department directs filings through ComOnline. Section 80C.08 gives 12 months from the Commissioner’s order, with the prescribed annual report before that period ends.

sections.heading: Deliver the buyer’s package under both applicable rules
paragraphs: For a franchise subject to state registration requirements, section 80C.06 subdivision 5 and agency guidance require the current public offering statement and all proposed agreements at least seven days before the earlier execution of a franchise or other agreement or payment of consideration—money or other value.

Obtain the signed acknowledgement before agreement/payment and retain it for three years from taking it. The independent federal 14-calendar-day requirement applies where covered; seven state days do not shorten it.

sections.heading: A signed sale may not release its initial fee
paragraphs: Where adequate financial arrangements have not been demonstrated, the Commissioner may require escrow, impoundment or fee deferral; guidance also describes a surety-bond alternative and deferral until the operator opens. These are possible actual-review conditions, not universal restrictions. Escrow or impoundment holds the funds under specified conditions; deferral postpones collection or availability. A surety bond is a guarantee from a surety company under its stated terms.

If the fee is unavailable until opening, it cannot fund earlier training or travel without another usable source. The support-funding companion explains that cash gap. Read the actual condition and release terms.
Registration expiry does not decide contract renewal, termination or transfer; the separate relationship guide addresses those actions.

practicalOutput: Establish registration or exemption before a covered offer, then schedule buyer delivery and check any actual fee-release condition.
limitations: Actual fee exclusions, sector exceptions, exemptions and financial conditions are not determined here. Agreement changes and delivery facts also need application to the transaction.
editNote: Owner question: When may I offer a Minnesota franchise, and what must the buyer receive before committing? Subtractive decision: Move “Check when initial fees can actually be used”, the German training-funding example and escrow/deferral glossary detail to the existing support-funding companion. Keep a short conditional assurance warning and link here; remove the repeated final combined-plan instruction. Final focus: Make this the concise Minnesota pre-sale page: coverage/exemption, effective order, buyer package and acknowledgement. Use the separate funding and relationship pages for their distinct owner decisions.

learningSummary: Hawaii’s filing instructions require the seller’s names, financial statements, funding information and consents to describe the same offering. This page addresses those filing errors; it does not establish when an offer may begin.

sections.heading: Submit the right package for the actual seller
paragraphs: Hawaii’s Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs (DCCA) directs franchise filings to the Securities Online Portal. Its tips call for the required materials together under the relevant initial, renewal or amendment category, with the associated fee.

If a U.S. subsidiary will sell the franchises, its application, Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD), agreements, seller information, costs and source-of-funds material must describe that arrangement. A parent’s accounts or name do not establish a commitment to fund the subsidiary’s promises.

For example, Form B showing parent-company costs and accountant consent referring to a different statement set need correction against the actual seller, obligations, funding company and accounting periods. Any proposed parent guarantee must name the right parties and statements.

sections.heading: Check consents and overseas signatures
paragraphs: The tips call for Form C to be notarized by a U.S. notary. They also call for signed, dated accountant consent from a qualified certified public accounting (CPA) firm, referring to the correct statements and relevant guarantor statements where applicable.
Confirm the currently accepted notarization process before arranging signatures abroad; an ordinary signature is not necessarily equivalent.

sections.heading: The 120-day position does not settle offer timing
paragraphs: DCCA currently links Interpretive Order 2023-1, dated April 19, 2023. It describes the underlying 90-day financial-statement requirement and says the Commissioner will take no action to require 90-day currency if the statements are current within 120 days of the registration application. It remains effective until amended or rescinded by another interpretive order or rule. This is the stated no-action position, not a claim that every financial-statement condition has been removed.

The agency’s fee table lists $250 each for franchise initial filing, amendment and renewal. Those fees and the statement-age position do not establish when a covered offer may begin or what buyer delivery requires.

practicalOutput: Correct seller and statement mismatches, then confirm current execution, statement-age and offer-timing requirements before relying on the filing.
limitations: Limited to filing preparation, the cited fee table and Order 2023-1’s conditional no-action position. Complete registration/effectiveness, buyer-disclosure, exemption and current execution requirements remain unresolved.
editNote: Owner question: Which company and financial statements should appear consistently in my Hawaii filing? Subtractive decision: Cut “Reconcile the mismatches before inferring anything from the filing” and the role-allocation columns in “Use one consistency sheet”. Shorten the CFO/company-secretary narrative; move the unreviewed-age limitation next to the financial-statement instruction, not another long ending. Final focus: Present a limited filing-error guide, not a Hawaii launch guide: identify the seller, align the statement references and explain exactly which current acceptance/age/timing questions it does not answer. Source follow-up: Read the complete currently linked order: the120-day financial-statement no-action position and listed filing fees are now sourced. Complete offer/effectiveness/disclosure rules remain unverified.
conditionsRetained: Correct initial/renewal/amendment category and associated fee.
Form C U.S.-notary instruction, current accepted execution needs confirmation.
Qualified CPA signed/dated consent; correct statement set and relevant guarantor.
Parent funding requires actual commitment, not ownership/accounts alone.
Unreviewed 2023 statement-age order; no established offer date or complete exemption/registration trigger.
Source follow-up scope: Complete registration trigger, effectiveness, buyer delivery, exemptions and current overseas execution acceptance remain outside the recovered scope.

learningSummary: Illinois’s published filing forms do not mean every applicant must use every assurance arrangement. Match the actual seller’s obligations to the funding or guarantee being proposed; this limited note does not establish initial offer timing.

sections.heading: Parent accounts are not a funding commitment
paragraphs: The Attorney General’s Franchise Bureau publishes application, costs/source-of-funds, seller, consent-to-service, guaranty and accountant-consent forms, plus escrow, surety-bond and deposit documents. Their availability does not establish that every form is required or a proposed guarantor will be accepted.

If a new U.S. seller promises training funded by a Swedish parent, identify the seller’s actual obligations, when costs fall due and the parent’s actual commitment. Parent financial statements alone do not commit that money. Accountant consent must refer to the correct statements.

sections.heading: What the annual tips sheet actually says
paragraphs: The currently linked annual sheet states renewal is due 120 days after financial year end. It calls for consistent issuance dates across cover, certification, accountant consent and receipts; clean and blackline (changes marked) FDD versions; and relevant forms, including revised Forms B and C where changes occurred.
It describes requesting removal of financial assurance in filing correspondence. A request is not an automatic release; the actual requirement and response control.

sections.heading: Confirm the current channel before submitting
paragraphs: The annual sheet is undated and contains hardcopy, flash-drive and no-email instructions. The currently accepted channel and fee were not verified. The cited preparation material also does not establish complete initial offer/sale timing, exemption tests, advertising, relationship or broker duties.

practicalOutput: Confirm the assurance actually required and the current submission instructions before relying on a proposed filing or annual renewal.
limitations: Limited to the cited document-preparation and annual-sheet instructions. Initial timing, current fee/channel and complete exemption or relationship rules remain unverified.
editNote: Owner question: Does my parent company’s money satisfy the funding support requested for the U.S. seller? Subtractive decision: Delete “Distinguish four different funding statements” and “Assemble a finance-and-document package”. Collapse the Swedish-parent example and funding prose into the one distinction between parent accounts and an actual commitment; move the undated-channel caveat beside that instruction. Final focus: Label this a limited assurance-document and annual-renewal preparation page, stating what a parent’s accounts do and do not establish without presenting it as an Illinois pre-sale answer.

learningSummary: For Maryland’s specified D–G registration exemptions, buyer documents can be due at the first personal sales meeting—not simply a set number of days before payment. Establish the exact exemption and any contrary order before inviting the prospect.

sections.heading: Registration relief is not relief from every duty
paragraphs: Business Regulation section 14-201 includes express/implied, oral/written arrangements with a substantially prescribed marketing plan/system, substantial brand association and a direct or indirect fee, including area franchises. Goods/services payments can count, subject to specified wholesale, fair-market-value and other exclusions.

Section 14-214 requires registration before covered offers, including advertising, or sales unless excluded or exempt. COMAR 02.02.08.10 has particular exemption routes. For D–G, absent a contrary order, deliver the offering circular and proposed agreements at the earlier of the first personal meeting or ten business days before signing/payment; specified routes also have notice conditions.

The regulation uses older Uniform Franchise Offering Circular terminology. A newer Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD) name does not remove its earlier meeting trigger. The independent federal period must also be met. Moving a Belgian prospect’s payment later would not remove an applicable first-meeting condition.

sections.heading: If registration is required, these are different events
paragraphs: Use the actual route and order conditions; these are not one universal timetable.

rows: Absent a stop order, noon on the thirtieth business day after the application or last amendment filing, or earlier Commissioner-set time. A filing receipt is not itself effectiveness.
Normally the first-anniversary regime, with materials at least 15 business days before expiry, subject to order and other conditions.
Prompt amendment; if approved, the Commissioner sets its effective date. No fixed 30-day allowance is supplied.
For an offering subject to registration, submit covered advertising at least five days before anticipated initial use.

sections.heading: Check sale-conditioned waivers separately
paragraphs: Section 14-226 bars requiring specified release, assignment, novation, waiver or estoppel arrangements relieving a person of statutory liability as a condition of sale. These can surrender, transfer, replace or prevent assertion of rights. The provision does not decide every later settlement, termination or choice-of-law issue.

practicalOutput: Before a personal sales meeting, identify the precise exemption or effective registration route and the documents and notice it requires.
limitations: Exact exemption, fee exclusions, orders and current agency instructions need application to the offer. The legacy meeting trigger is preserved; the waiver rule is limited to its stated sale condition.
editNote: Owner question: If my Maryland offer is exempt from registration, can I meet the buyer before delivering documents? Subtractive decision: Put the conditional D–G answer and Belgian meeting example together. Use “Ask which clock belongs to this Maryland route” in place of the repeated filing/renewal prose; move the long UFOC expansion and side-paper vocabulary below the direct answer. Final focus: Answer the proposed meeting question first, then give a compact registration-versus-exemption reference. Treat annual administration and sale-conditioned waivers as secondary rather than equal introductions.

learningSummary: File Michigan’s annual Notice of Intent before a covered offer or sale. The agency states a $250 fee and one year from filing; this filing does not mean it has checked the buyer’s disclosure documents.

sections.heading: What to file and when
paragraphs: MCL 445.1507a requires annual notice before offering or selling in the state. The Attorney General describes the Notice of Intent, $250 fee and one-year effectiveness from filing, repeated annually.
The agency says it does not review Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD) compliance. A filing on record is not approval, recommendation or endorsement of the opportunity.

sections.heading: Check the actual arrangement
paragraphs: The agency quotes a definition combining a substantially prescribed marketing plan/system, substantial association with a commercial symbol and a direct or indirect required franchise fee, including oral/written and express/implied arrangements. Fee exclusions and other scope conditions require their own facts.
The full current section 445.1502 and 445.1527 routes were blocked in the recorded review; complete exceptions and ongoing-contract analysis are not claimed.

sections.heading: The annual notice does not replace buyer delivery
paragraphs: MCL 445.1508 requires disclosure, the prescribed Michigan page/prohibited-term notice and proposed agreements at least ten business days before the earlier binding agreement or consideration (payment or other relevant value). The independent federal period is fourteen calendar days where applicable.

A deposit before the main signing date may be the earlier event. Do not convert ten business days to a fixed calendar count or assume a holiday’s treatment. The linked timing note explains the remaining inputs.

practicalOutput: Complete the required annual notice before a covered offer and check buyer delivery separately before taking money or signing.
limitations: The definition is the agency’s quotation; full current exception and prohibited-provision routes were unavailable. Actual fee exclusions, exemptions, offer connections and ongoing-contract rights remain unresolved.

learningSummary: One planned Indiana operator is not automatically an exemption. Unless the actual exemption conditions are established, the agency requires registration before a covered offer or sale.

sections.heading: A pilot still needs the state test
paragraphs: The Securities Division quotes a substantially prescribed marketing plan/system, substantial commercial-symbol association and a required franchise fee. Examine actual operating requirements, brand use, payments and fee exclusions rather than a licence label.

The agency describes limited-sales, large-net-worth, franchisee-sale and rule/order exemption routes. The claimant bears the burden. They are described as self-executing, meaning their conditions—not agency silence—must be established. An optional determination-letter process is available; another state or federal exemption is not the Indiana answer.

sections.heading: Registration is effective on receipt only under the stated condition
paragraphs: The Division describes initial registration as effective upon receipt if no stop order is in effect, lasting one year. It calls the process notice filing without merit review; this does not certify earnings claims or investment quality.

sections.heading: Renewal and changed documents have separate triggers
paragraphs: The agency lists a $500 initial fee, current Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD), seller disclosures, consent to service and supplemental materials. Renewal is due no later than expiry; a lapse requires initial filing and fee.

Its guidance requires an amended FDD within 30 days of a material change. Before giving prospects a new FDD, file it as an update to the effective registration or submit an explicitly requested early renewal. An annual reminder alone does not satisfy those tasks.

practicalOutput: Before presenting the pilot offer, establish the specific exemption or complete the required registration; then apply the new-document and renewal rules.
limitations: The current agency instructions were read, but statute links used a 2024 path and the attempted current legislature PDF was an application shell. Full current relationship-law coverage was not retrieved.

learningSummary: “Two weeks after delivery” does not prove a Michigan franchise deposit is timely. The state uses ten business days; the independent federal rule uses fourteen calendar days where it applies.

sections.heading: Count against the earlier relevant commitment
paragraphs: Michigan section 445.1508 requires the disclosure statement, prescribed Michigan notice and proposed agreements at least ten business days before the earlier binding agreement or consideration—payment or other relevant value.

The federal fourteen-calendar-day requirement is separate. Include every proposed agreement and state page, establish the legally relevant delivery facts and compare both applicable periods with their triggers. A later main signing does not automatically fix an earlier deposit.

Near a holiday, calendar days and legally counted business days may produce different results. This note supplies neither holiday rules nor an automatic legal delivery date; those inputs must be resolved before using the proposed commitment date.

sections.heading: A receipt must identify the package actually delivered
paragraphs: Use the actual recipient, document version, delivery method and delivery/receipt facts. If a Michigan page or agreement version is missing, or a later agreement changed, that uncertainty remains; the worksheet cannot determine the legal effect of an amendment or negotiation.
The annual Notice of Intent is a different seller-level duty, explained in the Michigan notice guide.

practicalOutput: Resolve missing package, delivery and holiday inputs before relying on either calculation to schedule a deposit or signature.
limitations: This is a limited timing explanation, not a determination of legal delivery, holiday counting, agreement-change effects or exemptions. Annual filing, advertising and relationship rules are separate.

learningSummary: If an actual Minnesota assurance condition postpones an initial fee until opening, that fee cannot pay an earlier training bill. The practical question is how much usable money you have before the fee is released.

sections.heading: Read the actual restriction first
paragraphs: The guidance describes escrow, impoundment, a surety-bond alternative and fee deferral where adequate financial arrangements have not been demonstrated. The Commissioner may impose the applicable protection; not every applicant has the same condition.
Use the actual order, agreement and release terms. An expected fee or revenue recognized in accounts is not necessarily cash you can spend.

sections.heading: One fictional calculation
paragraphs: Suppose, only for illustration, training travel and wages require $12,000 in month one, while the initial fee becomes available in month three. With no other committed receipt usable earlier, the month-three fee cannot pay the month-one bill on time.

Start with the $12,000 plus other actual dated outflows and reduce the gap only by committed receipts usable in that period. Do not count the expense and an identical arbitrary reserve twice. The $12,000 is not a Minnesota fee, capital minimum or required reserve.

sections.heading: A delay can extend the gap
paragraphs: If release depends on opening, a later opening can extend the period requiring separate capital. Testing a later date is an optional planning exercise, not a prediction of the regulator’s condition. A forecast opening date is not evidence that the release event occurred.
Confirm actual funding availability, costs and restrictions, and the actual release evidence before treating the fee as usable.

practicalOutput: Compare pre-opening payment dates with cash actually available under the selected condition; arrange any funding gap before promising support.
limitations: Release requirements depend on the actual review and arrangement. The fictional calculation predicts neither an assurance condition nor an approved funding level.
editNote: Owner question: How do I pay pre-opening support costs if my initial franchise fee is unavailable until opening? Subtractive decision: Delete “Put the existing illustration on a cash-date line” or use it instead of the three-paragraph example, not both. Cut “Give finance a short, verifiable file”; retain the delayed-opening point as clearly optional business planning. Final focus: Use the stated fee restriction to explain the financing gap, then show the arithmetic once. Separate the actual order’s legal conditions from the owner’s optional downside forecast.

learningSummary: Alabama’s named religious-day law restricts specified opening requirements for covered operators, subject to distinct agreement exceptions. An existing agreed term and a new instruction are not the same situation.

sections.heading: Who and what the Act covers
paragraphs: Act 2026-591 addresses a covered operator’s sincerely held religious belief about operating on a particular day. The enacted SB 138 text gives June 1, 2026 as the effective date; the fiscal note identifies the enacted Act.

Its agreement definition includes a writing, amendment or renewal, and a course of practice involving a brand licence and franchise fee where there is no writing. Incorporated manuals can matter. Its franchisor and franchisee definitions use their own product-arrangement wording and nonidentical regulated-business exclusions; service-only coverage remains unresolved here.

sections.heading: Compare the actual agreement history
paragraphs: The Act separately treats conspicuous operating-day terms in the original or then-existing agreement, requirements accepted through agreed renewal or amendment, and agreements expanding the operator’s number of locations. These are distinct exceptions, not a blanket permission for every later term.

If you add weekend emergency response to a maintenance manual after an objection, examine whether the relevant requirement was already conspicuous in the agreement or was accepted in a qualifying later agreement. An optional alternative call-cover arrangement can help customers, but is not itself a legal exception.

sections.heading: A remedy requires the statutory finding
paragraphs: Section 1(d) allows specified damages, reasonable legal fees and costs, injunctions or other equitable relief and civil penalties after the court’s stated reasonable-cause finding. An objection alone does not establish an automatic payment or penalty.

practicalOutput: Check the parties’ statutory coverage and the actual opening-days term before enforcing the schedule or deciding renewal.
limitations: Service-only coverage is unresolved, and the recorded review did not comprehensively search later injunctions. This is the named opening-days law, not a general right to close on any chosen day.
editNote: Owner question: Can I require an Alabama operator to work a day they object to on religious grounds? Subtractive decision: Keep either “Read the exceptions against the actual documents” or the three-row comparison, not both. Cut “Prepare one agreement-history file” and shorten the general discussion that opening days affect staffing and customer value. Final focus: State the conditional restriction and who it covers, then explain why an existing agreed term differs from a new instruction. Do not turn a scheduling alternative into a legal exception.

learningSummary: Alaska’s business-opportunity chapter excludes “a franchise under 16 C.F.R. Part 436.” Establish that actual exclusion first; the covered business-opportunity registration timetable is not automatically imposed on an excluded franchise.

sections.heading: Choose the actual statutory route
paragraphs: Section 45.66.220 contains the federal-franchise exclusion and others, including a separate trademark/financial-condition provision. Do not add an invented Alaska notice, fee or compliance condition to the quoted federal-franchise exclusion. A licence label or foreign mark alone does not establish another exclusion.

Section .900 separately defines specified device-location/customer-account assistance, buyback, assured-income/refund and marketing-plan arrangements. Section .070 examines offer origin/receipt, communicated acceptance and the stated buyer-domicile/operating-location connections. Being excluded from this chapter does not remove independent federal duties.

sections.heading: If the chapter applies, count from the actual event
paragraphs: The covered filing package includes the disclosure statement, promotional material, required bond, consent to receive legal documents and application. The regulation adopts forms revised February 9, 2005; that age does not itself invalidate adopted forms, and no new online route was established.

rows: Sections .010–.020(c) and 9 AAC 16.010: registration is complete when the seller receives acknowledgement; it must precede the sale or offer by at least 30 days, not merely be sent 30 days earlier.
Section .080 and 9 AAC 16.020: at least ten calendar days before the specified earlier contract-signing or receipt-of-consideration event; any independent federal period remains separate.
Annual renewal by the initial acknowledgement anniversary under .030.

Statement within ten days under .050; 9 AAC 16.060 specifies the adopted form and hand delivery or certified mail. Examples include payment, management/ownership, obligations, bond and significant litigation changes.
9 AAC 16.030: throughout offers/sales and three years after the last sale, not just until promotion stops.

sections.heading: Covered contracts have cancellation rights
paragraphs: Section .090 requires a written contract with specified terms. Under .130, the buyer can cancel for any reason by written notice within 30 days after signing, with additional cancellation grounds also provided.

Within 15 days after notice, the seller must refund payments and end the buyer’s financial obligations. Within five days after receiving the refund, the buyer must make supplied products, equipment or supplies available. Section .170 prohibits and voids waiver of chapter rights or defenses. These are not automatic rights for every excluded franchise.

practicalOutput: Determine the exact exclusion before using the covered-route dates; if covered, base the offer date on received acknowledgement.
limitations: The served compilation is labelled Alaska Statutes 2025. The chapter and regulations were read, but later 2026 session laws and decisions were not comprehensively reviewed. Actual model, state connections and exclusion conditions remain necessary.

learningSummary: Arizona excludes a franchise as defined in the cited federal rule from this business-opportunity definition. If your arrangement remains covered instead, registration can be required before solicitation—not only before taking money.

sections.heading: A licence label does not choose the route
paragraphs: Section 44-1271(1)(c)(iii) excludes a franchise defined in 16 CFR 436.1. Compare actual brand association, assistance/control, payments and representations with that definition. Independent federal duties still apply where covered.

For a covered seller, section 44-1272 requires registration before soliciting from an Arizona location or soliciting a consumer located in Arizona. Both the sales team’s and prospect’s locations matter.

sections.heading: Use the deadline for the particular event
paragraphs: These duties belong to the covered-seller route, not every federally defined excluded franchise.

rows: Section 44-1276.01: stated disclosure at least five business days before the earlier specified commitment or payment event. Keep any independently applicable federal period separate.
Section 44-1272(A): annual renewal within the 30 days before expiry—not at least 30 days before.
Subsection B: generally a supplemental statement within ten days.
Subsection F: submit before use, including a changed sales script.

practicalOutput: Establish the exclusion or covered-seller route before approaching prospects or using revised sales material.

learningSummary: The identified 2023 Arkansas amendment was enacted; HB 1177 of 2025 was not. Neither a failed proposal nor an old disclosure document establishes the current rule for changing an operator’s transfer or exit terms.

sections.heading: What the reviewed records establish
paragraphs: Act 847 of 2023 amended the Franchise Practices Act’s application and added relationship provisions. The official marked text strikes the previous federal Franchise Rule coverage reference from the exclusion; deleted words are not a condition still to apply.

The legislature records HB 1177 of 2025 as having died in committee when the session adjourned. That proposal did not become an operative amendment through the bill. Preparing a Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD) does not establish exclusion from the enacted relationship law.

sections.heading: What remains necessary for an actual change
paragraphs: The enacted text addresses performance contemplating or requiring an Arkansas place of business and has stated exclusions. Its application provisions distinguish retroactive treatment from provisions applying to agreements entered into or renewed after the Act’s effective date.

There is no single assumed starting date for the whole Act. The actual provision, premises, original and renewal dates and claimed exclusions must be reconciled with current consolidated law and relevant decisions. That current application is not established by this limited review, including where a contract chooses another jurisdiction’s law.

practicalOutput: Use the enacted text rather than HB 1177; resolve the current provision and its agreement-date conditions before changing transfer or exit terms.
limitations: This is a limited enacted-versus-proposed update, not complete current Arkansas relationship or franchise-sales advice. Current consolidation and transaction-specific application remain unresolved.

learningSummary: Colorado generally voids covered worker noncompetes unless a statutory exception applies. Putting a restriction in a franchise manual does not by itself establish either that exception or the separate notice owed to the individual.

sections.heading: Separate the worker’s covenant from the operator’s agreement
paragraphs: The reviewed 2026 section 8-2-113 addresses restrictions on an individual’s compensation for labour. The employer, worker, work location and actual restriction matter; an entity-level brand agreement is a different question.

Exceptions have conditions involving compensation, trade secrets, extent of restriction and other defined categories. Separate confidentiality, customer restrictions and noncompetition by their actual conduct, duration, area and protected interest. A confidentiality heading does not establish a noncompete exception.

The 2026 PAY CALC Order, effective February 1, 2026, lists $130,014 annually for highly compensated employees. Section 8-2-113 defines the covenant threshold as the greater of the Division’s August 10, 2022 amount or the amount when the covenant is executed; do not use a later year’s number automatically for an older agreement. For the stated noncompete exception, annualized cash compensation must meet the applicable threshold both when entered and enforced, the covenant must protect trade secrets and be no broader than reasonably necessary. The customer-nonsolicitation branch uses sixty percent of that threshold and its own trade-secret/narrowness conditions. Both branches exclude the stated restrictions on medicine, advanced-practice registered nursing and dentistry. Compensation alone is not eligibility.

sections.heading: Notice is required only for an otherwise permissible covered covenant
paragraphs: A prospective worker must receive the required notice and terms before accepting employment. A current worker must receive them at least fourteen days before the earlier of the covenant’s effective date or the effective date of additional compensation or employment-term changes providing consideration for it.
The notice must be clear and conspicuous, signed and in a separate document with the required language. Correct notice does not validate an otherwise impermissible restriction.

The notice must accompany a copy of the agreement, identify it by name and warn that it contains a restriction on later employment, and point to the specific sections. Its language must be the language used about the worker’s performance. These form requirements do not validate an otherwise void restriction.

practicalOutput: Identify the actual worker restriction and permissible exception before preparing the separate notice and hiring timetable.
limitations: The published 2026 amount and statutory conditions do not determine the actual covenant’s enforceability. Apply the correct execution/enforcement dates and exception; entity-level covenants and other categories remain separate.

learningSummary: A parent’s federally registered mark does not alone show that your U.S. selling company can claim Connecticut’s marketing-program exclusion. Trace the permission to use and sublicense the actual mark to that seller.

sections.heading: What the seller must support
paragraphs: Form CT-BOIA-EX, effective September 30, 2025, asks whether the seller holds the federally registered mark, an assignment transfers it, or an owner’s licence permits use and sublicensing to franchisees or purchasers. Territory and permitted activity matter. A Malaysian owner, Singapore regional licensee and U.S. seller need the actual chain of permission; shared ownership does not fill a missing licence.

The Department posts claims but cannot approve or validate them. Section 65 places the exclusion/exemption burden on the person relying on it. The form and older guideline describe route/attachments differently, so confirm current directions.

Section 36b-61(2)(D) places the mark language in the marketing-program branch. Specified third-party device locations, buyback and stated income/refund guarantees have their own branches; a mark claim does not automatically answer those.

sections.heading: If the opportunity remains covered
paragraphs: Without an applicable exemption, section 36b-62 requires registration effective by commissioner order before offer or sale. Section 63 requires disclosure at least ten business days before the earlier contract or money/other-value event. A permitted federal-format document still needs the Connecticut cover and additional content.
Section 62(d) requires immediate material-change notice and appropriate amendments; section 79 requires renewal within 120 days after the seller’s financial year ends.

Section 67 requires documented data and disclosure of that data when income/earnings-potential claims are made. It addresses inconsistent advertising/spoken claims and prohibited references to Act compliance in advertising or prospect contact. Section 80 separately addresses false/misleading statements and material omissions within its scope. Section 65 relief does not automatically remove every sales-practice provision.

sections.heading: A mark claim is not an exit-law answer
paragraphs: Sections 42-133e–h have their own relationship definition without a stated federal fee element. Their ordinary 60-day, abandonment 30-day, specified real-property six-month and qualifying-conviction delivery branches, lease service and compensation conditions are explained in the linked exit guide; they do not create universal cure.
The base code and supplement index were examined, but later session laws and special industries remain separate questions.

practicalOutput: Check the U.S. seller’s actual mark and sublicensing rights, then test the other promises before relying on the claimed exclusion.
limitations: Confirm the current claim channel and attachments rather than treating the older guideline as current procedure. No complete brand clearance or every exemption/sales-practice outcome is determined.

learningSummary: A shorter exit clause is not the complete answer for a covered Delaware product distributor. Section 2555 states at least 90 days’ notice notwithstanding contrary contract terms, alongside the statute’s other relationship protections.

sections.heading: Check the product and Delaware business
paragraphs: Title 6, Chapter 25, Subchapter V defines the franchised distributor through specified product/distribution activities and an in-state place of business. Products are tangible items here. A service licence is not automatically covered, and a distribution-agreement heading does not automatically exclude it.

sections.heading: Notice does not establish the right to exit
paragraphs: For covered relationships, the law addresses unjust termination/nonrenewal, good cause and bad faith as well as the at-least-90-day notice. An Italian equipment supplier’s preference for a new distributor is not by itself proof of those statutory conditions.

Apply coverage to the actual local operation and product flow, then examine the proposed action, reasons and notice. A contract clause permitting an unconditional or shorter exit does not complete that inquiry.

sections.heading: The worker wording has a limited purpose
paragraphs: Section 2554’s worker-classification wording is limited to Title 19, Chapter 11. It is not immunity from every employment, tax or joint-employer rule. The distributor company, its employees and the brand’s staff remain distinct parties.

practicalOutput: Check the defined distributor relationship and statutory grounds before relying on the contract’s exit clause or sending notice.
limitations: Actual coverage, cause, bad faith, notice compliance and remedies are not decided here. The worker provision is limited to its named chapter, and general franchise-sales or specialized dealer rules remain separate.

Subtractive decision: Delete “Self-check the Italian supplier’s exit plan” and “Make the next review practical”. Final focus: Explain directly why a shorter contract term does not settle a covered distributor exit, then use the Italian supplier example once to distinguish business preference from legal cause/bad-faith questions.

learningSummary: Florida’s franchise exemption filing remains even though the agency no longer requires the former registration documents. A qualifying seller must complete the notice and fee step before the covered offer or sale.

sections.heading: The exemption still requires a notice
paragraphs: The reviewed 2026 section 559.802 conditions the exemption from Part VII on a franchise meeting the federal definition, a notice stating substantial compliance with applicable Federal Trade Commission (FTC) requirements, and payment of the set fee before the covered offer or sale.

The scope includes a franchise to be located in Florida or a Florida resident. For example, a Florida resident seeking an outlet in another state still raises the residence branch. A completed Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD) does not itself satisfy the notice requirement.

sections.heading: The annual fee and renewal period
paragraphs: The initial exemption lasts one year from notice filing and may be renewed annually. Use the actual filing date for that period.

The statute permits a fee of no more than $100. The official rule-reference page now supplies the incorporated FDACS-10500 application, including its modified January 2023 copy: it states a $100 annual filing fee, nonrefundable. The current agency page directs applications and renewals to its Consumer Services Licensing Portal; its signed-in workflow was not inspected. The older paper packet’s mailing directions are not presented here as the current online procedure.

sections.heading: A notice does not validate a sales claim

The linked representations guide explains that narrower question and the required civil showing for remedies.

practicalOutput: Establish the qualifying exemption and actual seller, then use the agency’s current portal and annual notice process before a covered offer.

learningSummary: Recording a Georgia business or trade name does not establish ownership of a trademark or authority for another group company to license it. Georgia’s state mark filing also does not complete a U.S. availability search.

sections.heading: Three different records answer different questions
paragraphs: The Secretary of State distinguishes a business/trade name (often called a DBA) from a trademark or service mark identifying goods or services. Identify which entity owns the actual mark and what permission the U.S. seller has to use and sublicense it.

For example, a Singapore parent’s company name, its U.S. seller’s trading name and the mark on training material can be different records. None substitutes for the licence allowing the actual seller to grant the proposed rights.

The current application instructions say the office does not search federal or other-state registrations and cannot guarantee availability. State acceptance is not a completed assessment of competing U.S. rights.

sections.heading: Current franchise-sales law is not established here
paragraphs: The Attorney General’s hosted business-opportunity text is labelled current through the 2006 Regular Session. It establishes historical wording, not current thresholds, exclusions or deadlines.

The linked trademark guides address the broader rights questions. Current Georgia business-opportunity coverage, filings, disclosure, advertising and relationship requirements remain unresolved; a name or mark record does not answer them.

practicalOutput: Check the mark owner and actual seller’s licence, and use current authority for any claimed Georgia sales-law exclusion.

learningSummary: Idaho has no general state business licence, but business registration is not permission to perform every service. Occupational, tax and city/county requirements can still apply.

sections.heading: What the official portal establishes
paragraphs: Business.Idaho.gov distinguishes company/business-name registration from occupational permissions, tax accounts and local rules. Its Business Wizard is not guaranteed complete; an omitted activity does not establish that the work is unregulated.

If a cleaning offer adds disinfection, pesticide application, electrical work or specialist maintenance, identify the exact task, person, equipment/substances and location before relying on a generic cleaning-business answer. This page does not determine the professional category or permission for those tasks.
An activity-by-authority checklist can help organize the questions, but is optional management preparation, not a licence or worker-status decision.

sections.heading: Opening checks do not settle the partner offer
paragraphs: The Attorney General’s general Consumer Protection Act guidance describes unfair competition and unfair/deceptive practices. Its application to a particular business-to-business partner transaction, statement or remedy is not established here.
Idaho-specific franchise filing and exemption analysis also remains unresolved. Company registration or an internally completed permit list does not resolve those sales-law questions.

practicalOutput: Confirm requirements for the exact added service and address before taking that work; do not treat a missing portal entry as permission.

learningSummary: Iowa’s disclosure exemption removes a specified requirement, not every pre-sale or ongoing-relationship duty. The consent filing and agreement-date rules still need their own application.

sections.heading: Which requirement does your route remove?
paragraphs: Current 2026 Chapter 551A distinguishes definition/exclusions in section 551A.1 from the franchise disclosure exemption in 551A.4. The registered-mark/net-worth exclusion in 551A.1(2)(b)(3) is a different route.

The franchise route exempts section 551A.3 subject to providing the specified document at the earlier first personal meeting or fourteen days before the stated commitment/payment event. Moving signature later does not remove an earlier meeting trigger.

Section 551A.7 separately requires consent-to-service filing before contract or sale—a method for receiving legal papers, not commercial consent by the buyer. Relief only from .3 does not itself remove .7. Federal Franchise Rule analysis remains independent.

sections.heading: Agreement date selects the relationship inquiry
paragraphs: Do not apply older Chapter 523H by default; it expressly limits agreements entered on or after July 1, 2000. Section 537A.10 addresses defined Iowa-operated franchises from that date, subject to location/premises or principal-office conditions and sector exclusions.
It contains transfer, encroachment, termination and other protections. This page identifies the applicable inquiry, not every substantive test for those actions.

sections.heading: Do not apply the 2027 change early
paragraphs: The official 2026 amendment table records SF 2497 sections 29 and 32’s signed change to section 537A.10(7)(c)(2), effective January 1, 2027. It was a future change at the recorded November 12, 2026 source review; signing did not make that wording the then-current rule.

practicalOutput: Name the exact exclusion or exemption and the duty it affects before arranging the first meeting or contract; check agreement-date scope for later operator changes.
limitations: No universal Iowa exemption or complete section 537A.10 relationship test is established. Actual location, sector and future-effective-date conditions remain material.

learningSummary: For Kansas entity registration, “foreign” means formed outside Kansas, including another U.S. state. Each company’s own activities determine the qualification question; a resident agent is a legal contact, not automatically its headquarters.

sections.heading: Check what each company actually does
paragraphs: The Secretary of State says non-Kansas businesses doing business in Kansas must register and provides foreign-entity forms. Applicable doing-business exceptions still need examination; a commercial connection alone is not a complete answer.

If a Dutch parent supplies brand/remote training while an independent Kansas partner signs customer contracts, invoices and employs technicians, those are separate roles. Planned parent project visits also require assessment; the partner’s filing does not answer for the parent.
Identify who contracts, receives money, employs or sends staff and controls premises. That factual description is useful preparation, not a determination of the detailed exceptions.

sections.heading: What the resident agent address means
paragraphs: Kansas One Stop describes a resident agent receiving formal legal papers (legal process) at a physical Kansas registered office. That contact is not necessarily a headquarters, customer site or outlet and does not itself require a parent to relocate or create another subsidiary.

sections.heading: Qualification does not decide tax or franchise sales
paragraphs: Entity registration does not settle tax connection, staff work permission or sector requirements. This page has not established Kansas franchise registration, exemption, disclosure, advertising or relationship rules; a filing receipt does not complete them.

practicalOutput: Assess each existing entity’s actual Kansas activities and applicable exceptions before choosing a foreign-entity form or agent.
limitations: Detailed doing-business exceptions and current franchise-sales/relationship rules are unresolved. No new subsidiary or headquarters move is recommended by the cited framework.

learningSummary: Kentucky’s qualifying franchise-exemption route uses the current notice portal and the actual offeror’s documents. Important changes need separate notification; a completed notice is not the end of the duty.

sections.heading: Use the actual seller’s current notice route
paragraphs: KRS 367.807(1)(a) links the exemption to the federal franchise definition, federal compliance and written notice. Current 40 KAR 12:410, effective June 30, 2026, directs section 3 notices through the Franchise Exemption Notice portal with authority-to-transact evidence and the offeror’s Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD).

Match the seller in the offer, authority evidence and FDD. A parent’s history does not establish a subsidiary’s authority. Older/redline material and former determination forms are not automatically the current process; registration, renewal and exempt-offeror routes differ.

sections.heading: Fourteen days does not override an immediate statutory duty
paragraphs: Current rule section 4 requires written notification within fourteen days of material changes by stated registered sellers and exempt-notice offerors. KRS 367.805(2) separately says a registered offeror shall notify immediately.
Preserve both instructions and apply the actual route. The regulation is not permission for a registered seller to delay an immediate statutory duty or wait for annual paperwork.

sections.heading: The nonexempt process is separate
paragraphs: For a covered seller without an established exemption, the rule requires approval before covered sales to Kentucky residents, electronic registration/renewal and supporting documents. This route has its own fees; approved registration/renewal lasts one year from written confirmation.

Its cancellation wording remains unreconciled: KRS 367.816’s prescribed notice says thirty business days, while 367.819 says thirty calendar days. Do not turn either into a single resolved deadline or apply the provisions automatically to an established franchise exemption.

practicalOutput: Establish the qualifying route, use the current seller’s portal documents and apply the appropriate notification rule when facts change.
limitations: Exemption eligibility and the nonexempt cancellation conflict are not resolved. A portal record does not establish advertising, relationship or industry-law compliance.
