learningSummary: A registered brand does not automatically exclude an equipment-and-buyback package from Louisiana’s business-opportunity rules. The actual promise determines which definition branch—and possible pre-promotion bond duty—needs examination.

sections.heading: Test the buyback or income promise separately
paragraphs: RS 51:1821 puts registered-mark wording within the specified sales/marketing-plan branch. Specified device-location help, product buyback and earnings/refund representations have separate conditions. Device placement is not every form of customer-finding or site advice.

For example, a German seller promising to buy back output if the operator is dissatisfied must test that promise separately from its registered mark. The actual payments and other conditions still matter.

sections.heading: When the bond requirement applies
paragraphs: RS 51:1822 requires covered bonds before conducting business, including advertising or soliciting. Subsections A and B require authorized-surety bond face amounts of $50,000 for a covered seller and $25,000 for a covered agent, including the stated independent contractor, broker or employee roles. These are bond amounts, not a quoted premium or application fee; the actual role matters. Subsection G limits the bond duty to opportunities defined in 1821(1)(a), (b) or (c), not every trademark licence.

For those opportunities, subsection H makes the bond continuous. The surety—the company guaranteeing the bond—can terminate through 60 days’ written notice to the specified assistant secretary and the principal, whose obligations the bond guarantees; liability continues during that period and for accrued pre-termination liability discovered later. Subsection E requires a new/additional bond before continuing business. The 60 days is a bond rule, not franchise-contract exit notice.

sections.heading: The agreement must reflect covered oral promises
paragraphs: For covered opportunities, RS 51:1823 addresses documented earnings support, specified ad disclosures, actual seller identification and appointment of the secretary of state for service of process.

Subsection (6) requires the written agreement to include material oral statements, representations and promises made before execution. Subsection (7) prohibits waiver of purchaser legal rights; signing does not erase the earlier sales conversation.

sections.heading: A separate rule applies to real-estate brokerage
paragraphs: RS 37:1465 prohibits the described franchisor from contracting with a Louisiana real-estate broker without appointing a Louisiana-licensed broker as state representative. Property maintenance is not automatically brokerage.

practicalOutput: Test the actual promises and seller/agent roles before advertising, then arrange any applicable bond and confirm its filing procedure.
limitations: Actual coverage, role and bond procedure require application. The stated bond face amounts do not quote an insurance premium; the limited bond and brokerage rules are not complete franchise or operating-law treatment.

conditionsRetained: Source follow-up scope: Actual covered role, bond purchase/premium and administrative procedure still require facts; no universal franchise bond duty.

learningSummary: For a covered Maine business opportunity, registration can be required before promotion and buyer disclosure can be due at the first face-to-face sales meeting. Waiting until signature can therefore be too late.

sections.heading: Start with the actual package
paragraphs: Title 32, Chapter 69-B addresses specified location assistance, buyback, earnings/refund promises and marketing assistance, subject to its wording and exceptions. The federally registered-mark qualification belongs to the marketing-program branch, not every other trigger.
An equipment-and-training offer with an independent buyback promise needs that separate coverage analysis before using the covered timetable.

sections.heading: Match the duty to its earliest event
paragraphs: The state timetable is independent of federal franchise disclosure.

rows: Section 4692 uses the earliest specified 72-hour pre-agreement/pre-payment event or first face-to-face sales meeting. Calling a relevant sales meeting informal does not remove the trigger.

Section 4698 allows the buyer to withdraw by written notice within three full business days following the contract day, with its goods/funds return provisions. Signature does not make all receipts irreversible.
Sections 4695–4697 have applicable security, registration and exception conditions; do not assume every seller needs the same arrangement.
Update the disclosure statement as material information changes under 4696; annual renewal is not the only update.
Section 4697: one year from effectiveness. Renewal needs current disclosure, required fee and qualifying security evidence; failure to renew expires registration.

practicalOutput: Check coverage before promoting, then compare the first sales meeting with the agreement/payment disclosure triggers.
limitations: The official PDF is current through October 1, 2026 and is not the officially certified annotated text. Current forms, certified wording and case-specific interpretation may need confirmation.
Exact coverage, exceptions and all return obligations are not determined here.

learningSummary: Letting a Massachusetts technician choose their hours does not establish independent-contractor status. After the individual-services threshold is met, section 148B requires all three contractor conditions—not a favourable answer to only one.

sections.heading: Identify whose services and alleged employer are at issue
paragraphs: Chapter 149, section 148B starts with an individual performing services. Apply that threshold to the actual relationship and relevant current cases before moving to the exception. A brand, operator company, owner and technician do not all acquire one status together.

A technician choosing a schedule and a brand remotely checking quality are relevant facts, not a finished classification. Compare contractual controls with actual instructions, supervision, payment and the customer-contract/invoice roles. A franchise or contractor label proves neither universal employee nor contractor status.

sections.heading: All three conditions must be satisfied
paragraphs: Once the services threshold applies, the contractor exception requires all three: the individual is free from control and direction under the contract and in fact; the service is outside the alleged employer’s usual course of business; and the individual is customarily engaged in an independently established trade, occupation, profession or business of the same nature as the service performed.
Choosing hours alone addresses neither the whole control inquiry nor the other two conditions. This framework does not resolve current franchise-specific case application.

practicalOutput: Identify the individual’s service and possible employer, then examine every applicable condition rather than relying on schedule choice or a contract label.
limitations: The services threshold and relevant current cases require application to the actual facts. This is not a franchisee/technician classification verdict, and other employment or tax tests remain separate.

learningSummary: Promising a territory and later ending an operator’s rights raise different Missouri rules. Accurate territory wording does not create immediate-exit rights, and the two laws have separate definitions.

sections.heading: Do the exclusive customer promises overlap?
paragraphs: Sections 409.1000 and 409.1003 have a business-opportunity definition/exclusions separate from the relationship law. For covered offers, prohibited practices include the specified investment, training/support, profit and contract-rights representations and assigning the same “exclusive” territory to multiple purchasers.

A Belgian brand retaining national accounts inside two local territories must describe which customers and rights each promise includes. A private map not explained in the pitch does not cure conflicting promises. Covered sellers must provide a written contract and not misrepresent termination, transfer or renewal provisions.

sections.heading: A later exit uses its own coverage and exceptions
paragraphs: Section 407.400 uses a definition involving a licence and shared commercial interest (community of interest), Missouri place-of-business condition and specific exclusions. If covered, section 407.405 generally requires at least ninety days’ written notice of cancellation, termination or nonrenewal.
Specified misconduct, abandonment, insolvency and bad-check exceptions need their actual conditions; alleging default alone does not establish an exception.

sections.heading: Do not borrow a neighbouring remedy
paragraphs: Section 407.410(1)’s double-consideration and attorney-fee wording concerns inducing participation in a pyramid sales scheme, not an ordinary franchise notice dispute.

Subsection (2) separately allows a franchisee harmed by missing required cancellation or termination notice to seek the listed damages, including lost reputation/customer value (goodwill), costs and appropriate court orders directing or preventing conduct. The loss must be connected to the missing notice. Coverage, the actual notice failure and actual loss still need proof; this page establishes no award or complete court application.

practicalOutput: Make the actual territory promises consistent before offering; use the separate relationship test before later relying on an exit exception.
limitations: This establishes neither a universal state disclosure period nor absence of registration. Actual coverage, exemptions, notice exceptions and full judicial remedies remain unresolved.
editNote: Owner question: Can I promise exclusive customers to two operators, and does a later default let me end their rights immediately? Subtractive decision: Cut “Keep a sales file and an exit file” and “Assign the next concrete review”. Replace the added table’s long pyramid row and repeated remedy prose with one precise warning; keep the two owner questions as clear subanswers rather than another records system. Final focus: Use the actual customer promise as the sales question, then a short, separate answer about later notice. Explain that correct territory wording does not create immediate-exit rights.

learningSummary: For a covered Montana construction-equipment dealership, a missed sales target alone does not settle whether quick replacement is permitted. Good cause, notice and correction are separate requirements; inventory repurchase has a separate scope.

sections.heading: Part 9 is about a defined equipment relationship
paragraphs: MCA 30-11-901 includes oral/written and express/implied arrangements with a shared commercial interest (community of interest) in construction-equipment distribution. Separate equipment rights, retail/wholesale roles and branded services; a service-agreement heading is not the full definition.

sections.heading: Cause does not replace the notice branch
paragraphs: Under 30-11-902, the grantor—the party granting dealership rights, such as the supplier—must establish good cause for covered termination, cancellation, nonrenewal or substantial competitive changes and bears the proof burden. A contract clause or missed target does not itself establish it.

Section 903 generally requires 90 days’ prior notice by certified mail and 60 days to rectify deficiencies. Nonpayment has its own ten-day notice/remedy rule. Specified insolvency, assignment-for-creditors and bankruptcy grounds have different notice treatment under subsections (2)–(3). An alleged financial difficulty is not automatically a listed event.

sections.heading: Part 7 is a separate inventory test
paragraphs: Part 7 has distinct definitions for inventory repurchase, including industrial/construction equipment and repair parts. Part 9 coverage does not establish every Part 7 condition.

Apply the qualifying contract, condition, price basis and exclusions to the actual items, using age, invoices, freight, title and condition evidence. The spreadsheet’s full value is not a proved recovery.

practicalOutput: Identify the covered relationship and actual action before choosing a notice branch; assess any stock repurchase independently.
limitations: Part 9 and Part 7 have separate scopes. General franchise and business-opportunity sales requirements remain unresolved; no actual cause, exception or inventory value is determined.
editNote: Owner question: Can I replace a Montana construction-equipment dealer quickly for missing its target, and what happens to its stock? Subtractive decision: Delete “Keep the relationship decision apart from the stock decision” and “Prepare the proposed-action file before sending notice”. Retain the part 9/part 7 distinction in one concise paragraph beside the stock discussion rather than repeating it throughout. Final focus: Answer why a missed target alone does not settle quick replacement; then distinguish the conditional notice process from the separate question of which inventory qualifies for repurchase.

learningSummary: A D.C. brand’s operating permission does not automatically cover a new operator or its premises. Corporate records, tax registration, premises permissions and the activity-based Basic Business License answer different questions.

sections.heading: What does “all permissions included” cover?
paragraphs: The Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection separates corporate/trade-name registration, tax registration, zoning or home-occupation/occupancy requirements, and the activity-based Basic Business License application.

If a training brand promises all permissions are included, identify the actual holder, activity and address of each permission. A licence held by the brand may not establish the operator’s own required permission; company registration does not settle use of the proposed premises.
An operating licence also does not establish franchise disclosure compliance. This page has not completed the D.C. franchise-sales requirements.

sections.heading: The sales-claim law has its own coverage
paragraphs: Section 28-3901 includes franchises/business opportunities in its goods/services definition but separately defines consumer, merchant and transaction. That inclusion does not decide every business-to-business purchase.

Section 28-3904 addresses covered material misstatements and omissions. Actual buyer, purpose, seller and transaction facts and current application notes matter; do not assume every printed change has the same implemented effect or every broad pitch has the same legal result.

practicalOutput: Before promising all permissions, check what each actual operator and address still needs and make the sales statement match those facts.
limitations: Consumer Protection Procedures Act coverage is not established for every B2B operator. This is not a completed activity-specific licence or premises review, and franchise-sales questions remain unresolved.

Final focus: Explain what the broad promise would need to mean for this operator and address. State the known separate process categories without implying a completed opening checklist or universal consumer-law coverage.

learningSummary: A Nebraska office and high expected branded income do not alone establish Franchise Practices Act protection. Its place-of-business and two sales tests must all be met.

sections.heading: Apply the state definition and every criterion
paragraphs: The Act has its own definition, including specific nonalcoholic-beverage wording, petroleum exclusion, franchise fee and good-cause concepts. A SAMP notice or federal franchise result does not decide this relationship question.
Section 87-403 requires all three criteria below; these are not general minimum sizes for entering Nebraska.

rows: The defined fixed place displaying/selling goods or offering/selling the franchisor’s services. Office, warehouse, storage place, residence and vehicle are expressly excluded.
Covered product/service gross sales exceeding $35,000 during the 12 months immediately before the lawsuit is filed.
More than 20% of the franchisee’s gross sales intended to be or derived from the franchise.

sections.heading: Coverage is not a promise of indefinite renewal
paragraphs: Section 87-404 generally combines good cause with written reasons at least 60 days in advance, with an abandonment branch and specified immediate-notice grounds. Noncompetition provisions have their own scope.

Section 87-404(1) also preserves a contract making the franchise nonrenewable or renewable only on stated reasonable conditions. Apply the actual contract, action and branch rather than treating 60 days as automatic permission or renewal as guaranteed.

practicalOutput: Test the exact premises and both sales criteria before relying on ongoing protections or choosing an exit procedure.
limitations: Actual definition, cumulative criteria, contract terms and exceptions require application. This is not complete Nebraska sales or operating-law coverage.
editNote: Owner question: Does our office-based service partner qualify for Nebraska’s ongoing franchise protections? Subtractive decision: Keep the tests in either “Apply all three statutory criteria” or “The travelling-service operator needs three separate answers,” not both at full length. Cut the table introduction’s repeated “figures are not general minimum business sizes”; reduce “Prepare the relationship decision file” because it restates the example and the template’s preparation box. Final focus: Lead with why the travelling office-based operator has not yet established protection, then give the three facts that determine that question. Keep exit procedure secondary to that coverage answer.

learningSummary: For Nebraska’s stated nonexempt SAMP earnings rule, multiplying accounts by assumed profit is not enough support for a purchaser-facing claim. The seller needs the prescribed actual-experience information and purchaser disclosure.

sections.heading: Establish the actual sales-law route
paragraphs: Section 59-1729 applies to covered seller-assisted marketing-plan earning-potential representations. Read it with the franchise exemption and other exclusions; this is not a finding that every marketing restriction survives for every qualifying exempt franchise. Federal financial-performance requirements remain separate.

sections.heading: A correct $4,000 calculation is not attainment evidence
paragraphs: The fictional calculation is 20 cleaning accounts × $200 monthly profit per account = $4,000 per month if the assumptions hold. It does not show purchasers obtained or retained those accounts or earned that profit.

The statute says multiplying sales by profit per sale is insufficient substantiation. Required information includes the seller’s selling history, number and percentage of purchasers forming the representation’s basis, and purchasers known to attain the stated results.
Identify the actual group, period and cost definition rather than converting selected inputs into a claim. An “illustrative” label does not supply missing support.

sections.heading: Keeping support is different from providing it
paragraphs: The rule addresses prescribed supporting data and disclosure to the purchaser. Apply the required step for leaving that data with the purchaser; an internal sales file alone may not satisfy it.
Nonexempt SAMP advertising also has applicable seller-identification requirements. Review the actual income message across slides, scripts, emails and calculators, not just one written version.

practicalOutput: Before using the figure with a purchaser, establish the applicable route, actual attainment support and prescribed delivery—not just the arithmetic.
limitations: This is the stated nonexempt SAMP branch. No future buyer result or universal exempt-franchise claims rule is established.
editNote: Owner question: Can we use “20 accounts at $200 profit” to recruit buyers, and what evidence is missing? Subtractive decision: Merge “What does 20 accounts multiplied by $200 establish?” with “Worked example: the cleaning-account package”; keep the calculation once. Cut the repeated “illustrative” warning and shorten “Make a claim-by-claim evidence file,” whose requested records already appear in the rule explanation. Final focus: Explain exactly what the arithmetic fails to prove and which actual purchaser records answer that gap, before discussing how the sales team stores documents.

learningSummary: New Hampshire’s dealer chapter can include specified industrial and other equipment, not just passenger cars. Adding machine sales or authorized service rights to a labour-only business can change which definitions need examination.

sections.heading: Identify the equipment and granted rights
paragraphs: RSA 357-C includes specified farm, utility, forestry, industrial, construction, yard and garden equipment. Its definitions also require particular sellers, rights and arrangements; the equipment list alone does not establish coverage.

Separate equipment sales, distribution, authorized service and warranty rights, including actual supplier and parts dependence. The specified single-line dealer exception and express treatment of service-only fleet, government or rental-vehicle arrangements need their own conditions.

sections.heading: This note does not supply an exit deadline
paragraphs: Covered relationships have good-faith, good-cause, notice and protest provisions. The actual RSA 357-C:7 route must be examined for the intended event. A contract saying “good faith” does not establish compliance, and this page supplies no universal notice period or compensation entitlement.

practicalOutput: Identify the added products and service/warranty rights before applying a dealer definition or choosing an exit process.
limitations: Limited to the named scope inquiry. Actual exceptions and the event-specific RSA 357-C:7 procedure remain unresolved.
editNote: Owner question: Does adding equipment sales and warranty work change the law relevant to our labour-only service offer? Subtractive decision: Cut the table’s introductory self-description and the worked example’s instruction to “make a table with one row for each activity.” Remove “This exercise has a commercial benefit even before the legal result is known”; move the generic protest/exit preparation out of the initial coverage answer. Final focus: Frame this as an initial screen: what changed when the operator gained machine-sales and warranty rights, and which specific exception question is still unanswered.

learningSummary: For Texas unemployment tax, an independent-contractor label or 1099 does not decide status. The Texas Workforce Commission (TWC) examines actual work and the right to control it, even if that right is not exercised.

sections.heading: Compare the reserved right with actual work
paragraphs: TWC’s Texas Unemployment Compensation Act guidance examines service, wages and direction/control. An agreement, business name or federal reporting form does not replace that inquiry.

If a cleaning company fixes routes and methods, supplies equipment, requires training and pays a weekly amount, those facts raise control questions even under a contractor agreement. Compare who may change methods, use helpers/substitutes, serve other clients and bear expenses or profit/loss. The example is not a classification verdict.

sections.heading: Twenty factors are not a points test
paragraphs: TWC’s comparison addresses instructions, training, business integration, personal service, helpers, continuing relationships, set hours, full-time requirements, work location, sequence, reports, payment, expenses, tools, investment, profit/loss, multiple clients, public availability, discharge and quitting.

Not every factor applies or has the same weight. Eleven favourable answers are not a pass mark. Relevant contract clauses and actual schedules, communications, invoices or work practices should explain mixed facts. A role change can require reassessment.

practicalOutput: Assess the actual role and retained control before contractor onboarding; keep federal tax, wage and other legal classifications separate.
limitations: Limited to Texas unemployment tax. Actual worker, entity, worksite, industry and date facts remain necessary; no result transfers automatically to another law or role.
editNote: Owner question: Does calling a cleaner a contractor help if we control the route, methods, training and tools? learningSummary: For the cited 2026 wage posters, the general regional rate is $17 in New York City, Long Island and Westchester, and $16 elsewhere. Worksite, industry and actual role—not headquarters—determine which requirements you must examine.

sections.heading: Use the worksite and 2026 dates
paragraphs: The miscellaneous-industry and building-service posters cover January 1 through December 31, 2026. In the fictional comparison, 30 covered hours at $17 is $510 and at $16 is $480: a $30 difference before other pay obligations.
Those regional figures do not establish every worker’s pay or an all-in labour cost.

sections.heading: Do not import another role’s pay exception
paragraphs: The building-service poster separately addresses residential janitor unit/weekly pay and an overtime exception. Cleaning a commercial building does not automatically qualify for that treatment.

The miscellaneous poster has its own extra-pay/credit notes and no tip credit. A restaurant hospitality credit cannot be assumed to apply. Check overtime, uniform maintenance and applicable call-in/spread-of-hours provisions under the actual industry and role.

sections.heading: The 2027 announcement is separate
paragraphs: At the recorded review, the Department of Labor overview displayed a 2027 table and announced the standard $17/$16 rates would remain under an off-ramp, the mechanism affecting a scheduled rate increase, while separately announcing a home-care increase and describing a Governor’s off-ramp proposal.
An announcement and a proposal are different records. Use the dated posters for 2026 work and recheck enacted law/current guidance for 2027 rather than treating the proposal as adopted.

practicalOutput: Choose the actual worksite, year and worker category before calculating the rate and additional pay obligations.
limitations: Limited to the named wage-planning issue. No actual classification or overtime exemption is decided; the 2027 announcement/proposal distinction remains material.

Subtractive decision: Keep one version of “Select the worksite before using the example’s arithmetic” and “Worked example: two otherwise similar weekly budgets”; do not repeat $510, $480 and $30 in both. Move “Keep 2027 information and proposals distinct” and “Off-ramp” out of the main 2026 explanation into a clearly dated end note. learningSummary: For qualifying Montana new-motor-vehicle dealers, access to warranty information does not automatically authorize access to the entire customer list for marketing. Data permission and ending a software contract are separate decisions.

sections.heading: Identify the business and the requested data
paragraphs: Section 30-11-717 uses the new-motor-vehicle dealer definition in 61-4-201. An ordinary service franchise, repair shop or used-only dealer is not shown to qualify merely by using dealer software.

Sections 717(9) and 719 distinguish required manufacturer data for specified transactions, warranty/recall work, performance and other listed functions. Marketing data is not automatically included. Section 719 also permits the stated compliant push/submission alternative rather than unrestricted direct entry into the dealer’s system.

sections.heading: Use the prescribed permission, not a broad software clause
paragraphs: Covered third-party access requires prior, express written permission in a document separate from other consent, contract or franchise writings. Identify sharing parties and required details, including what is shared, purposes and duration.

Section 718 also restricts access, use, sharing and specified technological/contract interference and addresses cyber ransom. Manufacturer, vendor and authorized-integrator roles can carry different duties.

sections.heading: Different clocks apply to consent and contracts
paragraphs: Under section 718, prescribed consent can be revoked/amended on 30 days’ notice without cause or immediately for cause. Sections 719–720 separately address vendor/integrator termination on their stated 90-day terms.

Transition conditions include usable electronic data, return/deletion following the dealer’s written directions, recipient lists and audit access. Successor access and lawful retention still need attention; a subscription end date alone does not settle permission.

practicalOutput: Separate required manufacturer fields from additional uses before granting access; apply the correct consent and transition terms when changing vendors.
limitations: Limited to the referenced new-motor-vehicle dealer provisions. Actual roles, statutory exceptions and other privacy, security and retention duties remain necessary.
editNote: Owner question: Does giving a manufacturer warranty data require handing over our whole customer list? Subtractive decision: Merge the first two rows of “Classify the requested feed before changing permission or vendors” into “Worked example: warranty information versus a marketing feed,” keeping one clear example. Avoid repeating both notice branches in the table and “Withdrawing access and ending a contract use different clocks”; move the unexplained cyber-ransom aside out of the central access answer. Final focus: Lead with whether each requested purpose is supported; treat withdrawing consent and switching the software vendor as distinct follow-on decisions rather than another round of register instructions.

learningSummary: Wyoming’s equipment buyback uses different eligibility and price rules for machines, parts, required technology and specialized tools. Even a correct valuation is not necessarily cash collected.

sections.heading: Confirm the dealer and each item
paragraphs: Chapter 40-20’s dealer definition combines selling/leasing to consumers and repair/service activities with stated exclusions. Owning a machine alone is insufficient; closing a covered location can also raise inventory issues under the agreement definition. Lawful termination remains a separate question.

Section 121 has conditions/exclusions for damaged packages, reconditioning, clear title, retained goods, condition, equipment delivered before the stated 36-month window, post-notice orders and other-source goods. Apply the actual qualifications: a damaged package is not always zero recovery.

sections.heading: Do not apply one percentage to every category
paragraphs: These section 120 figures concern qualifying items, with separate handling/freight and demonstrator conditions.

rows: Eligible new equipment; qualifying demonstrators separately conditioned
Ordinary equipment figure: 100% of net equipment cost.
Three-year straight-line acquisition-cost approach: spread acquisition cost evenly over the stated three years, subject to the minimum-specification qualification.

sections.heading: Return timing and payment start from different events
paragraphs: Section 121(a)(ix)’s return provision is tied to the later of effective termination and receipt of required return-policy information, with its notice qualification—not simply 90 days from any letter.

Section 120(b) generally requires payment or credit within 90 days after supplier receipt of covered property. The stated contractual signage-removal failure permits withholding. Outstanding sums can lead to account credit rather than cash; keep offsets and shared freight distinct.

In the fictional example, proved eligible $10,000 net equipment cost plus $2,000 qualifying current parts prices produces $10,000 × 100% + $2,000 × 95% = $11,900 before separate handling, freight, offsets and other conditions. That arithmetic does not establish technology/tool amounts, timely return or actual receipt/payment.

practicalOutput: Apply the actual item basis and return conditions, then distinguish the supplier’s receipt, any credit and cash payment.
limitations: Only the defined equipment-dealer branch is covered. No actual title, eligibility, return deadline, amount, tax treatment or recovery is determined.
editNote: Owner question: Which equipment and parts might be bought back, on what basis, and when would we receive cash or credit? Subtractive decision: Use the category explanation once: remove repetition between “Use the legal price basis, not one percentage for everything” and the first four rows of “Separate valuation rows from return and cash events.” Keep the $11,900 calculation once, and merge the table’s payment row with “Payment runs from another event”; reduce the six-bullet ledger prescription. Final focus: Structure the answer around recoverable category, qualified value and actual cash/credit trigger. Records matter only where they prove an item’s eligibility or the event starting payment.

learningSummary: In Washington, early termination and nonrenewal at expiry have different conditions and money consequences. A reasonable cure opportunity is not automatic permission to terminate on day 31.

sections.heading: Establish the state relationship and promised territory
paragraphs: RCW 19.100.010 uses the stated marketing-plan, brand and fee test, including oral/written and express/implied arrangements; required purchases/training and specified wholesale/property exclusions matter. Insurance and specified motor-vehicle treatment are separate. Neither “licence” nor federal classification decides it.

Section .180(2)(f) addresses competition and competitive grants where the agreement specifies an exclusive territory; it does not grant exclusivity to everyone. National accounts, online leads and actual service rights matter. Purchasing/conduct restrictions have separate reasonableness or business-ground tests.

sections.heading: Good cause and correction have distinct conditions
paragraphs: Section .180(2)(j) requires good cause for termination before expiry. Its ordinary default branch calls for written notice and a reasonable cure opportunity that need not exceed 30 days—not an unconditional minimum or automatic day-31 right.
If the problem cannot reasonably be cured in 30 days, the text separately addresses substantial and continuing corrective action initiated within that time.

The repeated-breach exception requires three willful and material breaches of the same term within twelve months, with specified prior notices/opportunities, then a subsequent willful and material breach of that same term within the same twelve months. Unrelated complaints do not establish it.
Adjudicated bankruptcy/insolvency, assignment for creditors, voluntary abandonment and the specified business-related criminal outcome have separate immediate-action conditions.

sections.heading: Nonrenewal has a different compensation rule
paragraphs: Section .180(2)(i) addresses fair compensation at expiry for listed assets bought from the franchisor and goodwill—the business value tied to established customer relationships and reputation—with exclusions and offsets. The goodwill exception requires both one year’s nonrenewal notice and a written agreement not to enforce a covenant restraining competition; it does not erase every listed asset obligation.
Good-cause termination has a narrower inventory/supplies purchase rule with a premises-retention qualification. Changing the action’s label does not establish the cheaper result.

practicalOutput: Identify the actual action and covered relationship before choosing a cure process or calculating expiry versus termination obligations.
limitations: No full damages, limitation, insolvency or litigation analysis is supplied. Section 190 remedies do not forecast an award; actual cause, compensation and exceptions remain conditional.
editNote: Owner question: Can we replace this operator before expiry, or decline renewal, and what compensation could follow? Subtractive decision: Choose either the new “Classify the action before selecting a process or ledger” table or the two preceding detailed exit explanations as the main version, not both. Move the general definition and territory/purchasing detail toward the existing Washington parent guide; cut the repeated “cheaper ledger” admonition from the example. Final focus: Begin with whether the intended replacement is early termination or expiry nonrenewal, then explain the different correction and financial consequences using the missed-target facts.

learningSummary: For a covered Wisconsin dealership, cause, advance notice and time to correct a problem are different requirements. A ten-day nonpayment remedy period does not establish an automatic day-11 right to terminate.

sections.heading: Registration does not decide Chapter 135 coverage
paragraphs: Chapter 135 includes the stated in-state dealership rights to sell/distribute or use a commercial symbol, express/implied and oral/written, with community of interest. This concerns the parties’ shared financial interest in the business relationship; whether it exists depends on the actual arrangement.

Section 135.07 excludes specified motor-vehicle dealers/distributors/wholesalers acting in that capacity, insurance and door-to-door marketing; liquor has separate provisions. Actual operation, not a brand label or federal fee test, determines the inquiry.

sections.heading: Use separate notice and correction tracks
paragraphs: Section 135.03 requires good cause for covered termination, cancellation, nonrenewal and substantial competitive changes, with the grantor—the party granting the dealership rights—bearing the burden.

rows: Ninety days’ prior written notice stating all reasons and sixty days to rectify. Timely correction voids the notice.
Written default notice and ten days to remedy from delivery or posting. The cited official jury-instruction comment preserves ninety days’ advance notice while shortening cure.
Specified insolvency, assignment for creditors or bankruptcy
Stated notice exceptions require the actual event and applicable conditions.

sections.heading: Repurchase is limited to qualifying marked resale stock
paragraphs: Under section 135.045, grantor-initiated termination can trigger repurchase at the dealer’s option, at fair wholesale market value, of qualifying inventory sold by the grantor for resale and bearing its identifying mark. A service tool or computer is not eligible merely because it helped run the business.
Section 135.06’s damages, costs/fees and injunction remedies have their own conditions; the provision is not an award prediction.

practicalOutput: Confirm dealership coverage and cause, then apply advance notice and correction independently before acting.
limitations: The older official jury instruction is used only for the specific notice explanation alongside current certified statute; no full appellate opinion was independently reviewed.
Complete community-of-interest case law, arbitration, federal preemption and liquor rules remain outside this guide.
editNote: Owner question: Can we terminate for nonpayment on day 11, or does advance notice still matter? Subtractive decision: Merge “Put advance notice and correction on different tracks” with the two preceding notice sections instead of printing both. Keep one explicit source-provenance note, preferably with source notes; cut the example’s generic file-collection narration and reduce “Prepare the action file.” Final focus: Answer the day-11 question immediately, explain what the shorter payment-correction period changes and what it does not, then give the separate inventory consequence briefly.

learningSummary: Virginia’s July 1, 2026 retail-franchise changes address governing law and specified post-term retail competition. Earlier registration does not by itself update the documents used for a later covered sale.

sections.heading: Apply the Act’s actual coverage
paragraphs: Chapters 553 and 554 took effect July 1, 2026. Section 13.1-559 requires the stated written retail marketing-plan/brand arrangement and a direct/indirect fee of $500 or more, subject to fee exclusions.

Performance must contemplate or require a defined Virginia place of business; incidental/ancillary and department exceptions have their actual statutory conditions. Calling an activity secondary does not alone establish one.

sections.heading: Review the two provisions separately
paragraphs: Section 13.1-559(D) requires Virginia law for franchise contracts offered/entered pursuant to the Act. Section 13.1-563(A)(4) prohibits offering/entering the stated restriction on franchisee retail offering, sale or distribution of goods/services after termination/expiry.

Section 563(B) permits the stated restriction when the franchisee sells to a third party or back to the franchisor at a mutually agreed price, for no more than two years after sale. Ordinary expiry or an unrelated payment does not establish that exception.
This is not a conclusion about confidentiality, intellectual-property or other distinct obligations.

sections.heading: A later sale may need amended documents first
paragraphs: The SCC’s April 14, 2026 notice calls for the language in the FDD (Franchise Disclosure Document) and agreement, through relevant Item 17 disclosure or a Virginia addendum.

For registrations begun before July 1 and expiring later, it distinguishes no expected Virginia sale before expiry from a possible/actual sale on or after July 1. The latter requires an amendment application first. A November offer using a pre-July template therefore cannot rely on registration age as proof of updated wording.

sections.heading: Clause updating is not an exit verdict
paragraphs: Section 13.1-564 separately restricts cancellation without reasonable cause and undue influence to surrender rights. Civil remedies and anti-waiver provisions have independent triggers; new wording does not decide an actual exit dispute.

practicalOutput: Check Act coverage, the actual clauses and planned sale date before using an older Virginia package.
limitations: No retroactivity or enforceability conclusion is made for agreements signed before July 1, 2026. Employee noncompetes, exemption/delivery rules and complete remedies remain separate.
editNote: Owner question: Can we use our pre-July template for a covered Virginia franchise sale later in 2026? Subtractive decision: Use “Compare the clause, exception and sale-document tasks” or the earlier rule paragraphs as the primary version, not both. Keep the November example’s facts in two sentences and remove repeated secretary narration; move “Contract updating is not a decision on an actual exit dispute” and the “Reasonable cause” glossary entry into a short scope note. Final focus: Lead with which two clauses and sale-document step an old package must be checked against; do not turn this into an exit-dispute or employee-noncompete guide.

learningSummary: An existing Oregon operator is not automatically excepted from disclosure when renewing, changing terms or buying another unit. Each transaction has its own conditions; revised support charges can matter.

sections.heading: Start with the actual franchise and sale
paragraphs: The reviewed 2025 ORS 650.005 covers stated oral/written marketing-plan, brand and valuable-consideration arrangements. A franchisor includes a subfranchisor selling for $100 or more to a franchisee/subfranchisor.
The sale definition separately excludes its stated unchanged, uninterrupted renewal/extension. That is not a blanket low-fee or amended-arrangement exemption, and federal tests remain independent.

sections.heading: Choose the transaction before the exception
paragraphs: A material adverse change means a significant change unfavourable to the operator, assessed under the relevant relationship or disclosure test. If no exception is established, OAR 441-325-0020 requires the disclosure and all proposed sale agreements at least fourteen calendar days before the earlier covered agreement or consideration, including refundable deposits.

rows: All three: no relationship-operation interruption; no material adverse relationship change; no material adverse change in previously supplied disclosure information.
Prior disclosure in connection with the earlier sale and no material adverse change in the supplied disclosure information. This is not the same renewal test.
No franchisor involvement, isolated sale and the specified fourteen-day full-record-access conditions.

sections.heading: The resale chapter exemption is separate
paragraphs: Rule 0040 describes the stated own-account/entire-area resale without franchisor participation or aid. Approval rights alone receive specified treatment; active marketing or help can change the facts.
This note does not reconcile every overlap between the resale provisions or approve a transfer.

practicalOutput: Compare the actual changed terms and disclosure with the earlier sale before claiming the transaction-specific exception.
limitations: Limited to the stated 2025 statute and disclosure rules, not motor-vehicle, fuel, recreational-vehicle or other relationship regimes. No current federal monetary exemption threshold is supplied.
editNote: Owner question: Must we give an existing Oregon operator fresh disclosure before selling a second territory with changed charges? Subtractive decision: Merge “Choose the Oregon transaction before using an exception” with the continuation/additional-franchise sections, keeping one account of each condition. Move “A resale is another distinct branch” and the table’s two resale rows out of the second-territory explanation; cut repeated change-log instructions from the example and final checklist. Final focus: Compare unchanged continuation with the added territory actually being sold, and explain why revised support charges require a change assessment rather than treating a familiar buyer as enough.

learningSummary: A qualifying Texas franchisor can be exempt from business-opportunity registration and still need Form 2703 notice before offering or selling. Identify the company actually selling the rights, not automatically the parent owning the mark.

sections.heading: The condition and prior filing are separate
paragraphs: The Secretary of State’s FAQ describes material compliance in Texas with applicable Federal Trade Commission disclosure requirements and prohibitions as the franchise exemption condition. It also requires the notice before the covered offer or sale.

Form 2703 asks for the franchisor’s legal name, every name under which it does or intends to do business, and principal business address. The FAQ lists $25 and describes a one-time notice without expiry, with principal-address changes notified in writing.
A completed Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD) or a “licence” contract heading does not establish the actual exemption and notice conditions. No expiry does not guarantee continued eligibility.

sections.heading: If the condition is not established
paragraphs: Nonexempt business-opportunity sellers have separate registration, disclosure and update processes. The one-time notice and $25 budget are not substitutes. Actual Texas communications and connections still matter.

practicalOutput: Establish the qualifying condition and actual seller, then complete the applicable prior notice before a covered offer.
limitations: Limited to the stated franchise exemption notice, not every Texas sales or operating duty. The actual model, offer connections and exemption conditions are not decided.
editNote: Owner question: If we qualify for Texas’s franchise exemption, what notice must be filed before the offer? Subtractive decision: Remove “Fill the Form 2703 decision card before scheduling an offer” or replace the preceding repetition with it, rather than retaining both. Reduce “Worked example: a facilities-services campaign” to the actual seller-versus-parent point; cut duplicate filing-evidence instructions in “Keep a clear pre-offer record.” Final focus: Give the qualifying seller the short form-and-timing answer, then state what happens if that exemption cannot be established. The filing record supports the step; it is not the main value proposition.

learningSummary: Washington’s franchise rules concern covered offers as well as sales. Registration, buyer disclosure, changed agreements and advertising have separate triggers; one completed filing does not satisfy them all.

sections.heading: Check the state arrangement before offering
paragraphs: RCW 19.100.010 includes oral/written and implied arrangements with the stated substantially prescribed/suggested marketing plan, substantial brand association and defined fee. Required goods/services and training charges can matter, with bona fide wholesale, property and other exclusions; insurance and specified motor-vehicle arrangements are separate.

Section .020 requires registration or exemption review before a covered offer. A licence heading, federal result or future outlet location does not decide all state connections. This is not complete business-opportunity-law coverage.

sections.heading: Keep the actual event and day unit
paragraphs: For example, a revised national-account reservation may change what a prospect was promised in both its agreement and an advertisement. Review each actual change and applicable branch.

rows: Seven calendar days; prospect-initiated negotiations have separate treatment.
File a true copy at least seven days before publication unless a shorter period is allowed.
Ordinarily one year from effectiveness/filing for the identified periods unless the director sets another period. Registration renewal is due no later than twenty calendar days before expiry.
Material adverse condition or material disclosure change
Amend as soon as reasonably possible and before another franchise sale; do not wait for renewal.

sections.heading: Territory and exit conditions are separate
paragraphs: RCW 19.100.180 addresses good faith, purchasing restrictions, exclusive territory, termination and renewal. A mandatory supplier or reserved national account therefore also needs its actual relationship-rule review. The exit companion explains the separate cause, cure and compensation branches.

practicalOutput: Check coverage before the offer, then apply the distinct delivery, amendment and advertising requirements to the actual versions and dates.
limitations: Actual parties, offers, state connections, exclusions and exemptions require application. Registration does not establish enforceability of a territory term or a later exit.
editNote: Owner question: What must happen before we offer, advertise, change terms or complete a Washington franchise sale? Subtractive decision: Use “Keep the event and the source’s day unit together” as the single account of the clocks and cut the duplicated timing paragraphs. Shorten “Worked example: an exclusive industrial-maintenance territory” to the changed-promise fact; reduce the operating-relationship section to a direct pointer to the existing exit guide. Final focus: Walk through the actual recruitment events and state what each requires, rather than narrating how several managers maintain records. Keep territory enforcement on its existing separate page.

learningSummary: A New York franchise sale can require registration and disclosure before the first sales meeting. Annual renewal is a separate duty; it does not replace buyer delivery, prompt amendments or advertising submission.

sections.heading: Register before a covered offer or sale
paragraphs: The Attorney General says offerings in or from New York must be registered before offer or sale unless exempt. General Business Law (GBL) 681(3) has alternative branches: a substantially prescribed marketing plan plus a required direct or indirect fee, OR substantial brand association plus that fee. Both plan and brand elements are not required in every arrangement.

Fee exclusions, area/subfranchise roles, uninterrupted renewals and state connections also matter. Part 200.1 adds fee and advice/training meanings. The actual rights, payments, support, offer/acceptance locations and proposed operation determine which branch or exemption needs examination.

sections.heading: Use the earliest applicable buyer event
paragraphs: GBL 683(8) requires the offering prospectus—the seller’s required buyer-disclosure information—and proposed agreements at the earliest applicable event below. Consideration means the relevant money or other value. The statute and the currently linked agency addendum use different day wording; that difference is not resolved here.

rows: The defined first face-to-face meeting to discuss a sale or possible franchise sale is an independent trigger.
GBL 683(8): binding franchise or other agreement
At least ten business days before the agreement.
At least ten days before receipt; the statute does not say business days here.
Uses ten business days alongside execution or related payment.
Fourteen calendar days where it applies; this does not remove an earlier state meeting or payment trigger.

sections.heading: Renewal, changed information and advertising
paragraphs: The agency guide directs annual renewal within 120 days after the franchisor’s fiscal year end. A fiscal year is its accounting year. The guide distinguishes timely pending renewal from expired registration: after expiry, no covered offers or sales within or from New York until renewal is submitted and accepted for filing.
The renewal package includes an updated Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD), marked changes, accountant consent, franchise-sales information, prices, credit terms and audited financial statements.

Part 200.5 separately requires prompt notification by an application to amend material prospectus changes, including the stated fee, significant adverse business/obligation/agreement/product or model, and financial changes. Do not wait for annual renewal.

The agency guide requires two advertising copies through FRED, the North American Securities Administrators Association’s franchise filing system, at least seven days before intended use. The advertising companion explains that separate submission.

sections.heading: Read waivers and side documents too
paragraphs: GBL 687(4)–(5) addresses waiver of statutory compliance and required releases, assignments, novations, waivers or estoppels relieving statutory duty or liability. These can surrender, transfer, replace or prevent assertion of rights; the signing context and exact wording matter. The provisions do not decide every later negotiated settlement.
The addendum also addresses preserved renewal/transfer rights, choice clauses and the stated limits on claim-waiver or reliance-disclaimer effects in commencement questionnaires and acknowledgments.

practicalOutput: Before scheduling the first sales meeting or accepting money, establish registration/exemption status and resolve the applicable delivery dates, including the statute/addendum difference.
limitations: The ten-day versus ten-business-day payment wording is preserved, not resolved.
Coverage, exemptions and state connections depend on the actual offer; this is not a complete operating-law review.
editNote: Owner question: When must we provide the FDD before a New York sales meeting, agreement or payment? Subtractive decision: Keep the source comparison in “Keep each source’s disclosure wording on its own row” and remove the repeated clock recital from “Disclosure can be due before the expected signing date,” retaining the complete-package/earliest-event explanation once. Cut generic finance/marketing narration from the worked example; move detailed “release, assignment, novation, waiver or estoppel” discussion away from the timing answer. Final focus: Answer the next planned meeting or payment first, explicitly identify the unresolved source wording, then state the separate renewal/advertising events without a fictional departmental choreography.
conditionsRetained: Alternative GBL 681 branches, exclusions, area/subfranchise, uninterrupted renewal and state connections.
Earliest specified first meeting, ten business days before agreement, ten days before consideration; April 2, 2024 addendum differs; independent federal 14 calendar days.
120 days from fiscal year end; expired status bars covered offers/sales until renewal submitted AND accepted for filing.
Prompt material amendment; advertising two copies through FRED at least seven days before intended use.
Waiver/side-paper scope and no universal later-settlement conclusion.

learningSummary: Virginia registration exemptions have different entity, transaction and filing conditions. An experienced overseas parent does not automatically make a new U.S. seller eligible, and registration relief can retain buyer disclosure. This page covers entity attribution and the stated filing/delivery dates; it does not set out the full exemption eligibility tests.

sections.heading: Match the condition to the actual entity
paragraphs: The State Corporation Commission (SCC) says covered Virginia offers/sales must be registered or exempt. Rule 21VAC5-110-75 includes unchanged uninterrupted renewal, additional existing-franchisee sales, seasoned-franchisor, institutional-buyer and substantial-investment routes.

Choose the exact provision before relying on group history, financial condition or buyer characteristics. Parent facts count only where permitted and any required guarantee is established; the seller cannot simply borrow the parent’s reputation.
For routes numbered 3–6, subdivision 7 retains the disclosure document and all proposed agreements fourteen calendar days before agreement/payment.

sections.heading: Advance filing and renewal depend on the route

rows: Specified Form H package at least ten business days before covered offer/sale; annual renewal rules apply.
Specified package at least ten business days before each offer or sale of each franchise.
Specific annual routes say at least ten business days before expiry; paragraph 8(c)(1) says ten days. Preserve and resolve that difference before relying on the shorter wording.
Exemption amendment is required. Electronic-media wording does not establish the exclusive current submission channel.

sections.heading: The exemption does not update contract clauses
paragraphs: The Act and SCC’s April notice require separate attention to the July 2026 Virginia governing-law and post-term retail-competition changes and negotiated-sale exception. The contract companion explains those conditions and amendment-before-sale instructions.

practicalOutput: Establish the precise exemption and required entity evidence before a covered offer, then meet its filing and retained delivery duties.
limitations: The ten-day/ten-business-day wording difference is unresolved. Actual offer, buyer, entity, exemption and current submission conditions require application.
editNote: Owner question: Can our new seller rely on group experience, and what filing and disclosure tasks remain under the selected Virginia route? Subtractive decision: Cut the duplicate “Use a route-and-evidence comparison, not the word exempt alone” or the preceding route/date sections. Remove its meta sentence “It deliberately does not supply the full eligibility test”; state that limitation plainly near the narrowed answer. Reduce the July 2026 contract discussion to the existing contract-guide link and drop unsupported glossary emphasis on self-executing routes not explained here. Final focus: Present a limited guide to entity attribution and the stated filing/delivery dates, not a route-selection or eligibility guide that omits the conditions needed to select a route.

learningSummary: Oregon does not require the franchise-document filing and prior approval described by its regulator, but buyer disclosure still applies to covered sales. “No filing approval” is not “no franchise law.”

sections.heading: Check the arrangement and Oregon connections
paragraphs: The Division of Financial Regulation (DFR) points to ORS Chapter 650 and OAR Chapter 441, Division 325, complaint handling and a conditional private civil remedy.

The reviewed 2025 ORS 650.005 uses marketing-plan, brand and valuable-consideration elements. Its franchisor definition includes a subfranchisor selling a franchise for $100 or more to a franchisee/subfranchisor; this is not a universal conclusion about low-fee arrangements.
Section 650.015 examines offer origin/direction, acceptance and stated domicile/operation facts. An outlet address alone does not settle those connections.

sections.heading: Deliver all proposed agreements in time
paragraphs: OAR 441-325-0020 requires disclosure and all proposed sale agreements at least fourteen calendar days before the earlier covered agreement or consideration, including refundable deposits.
Unchanged renewals, additional units and owner resales have distinct exception conditions. An existing buyer is not automatically excepted; the linked transaction guide explains those branches.

sections.heading: Retain the sale and proceeds details
paragraphs: DFR identifies complete books, records and franchise-sale details, including distribution of proceeds. The actual delivered documents, recipient/date, signed terms and money received help connect those required records to the sale; an unexplained bank total is not the whole record.

practicalOutput: Before an agreement or refundable deposit, establish coverage or the exact exception and deliver the complete package on time.
limitations: Based on the stated 2025 official statute and administrative rules, not every distribution, licensing or sector regime. Actual state connections and exceptions remain necessary; the civil remedy is not a predicted outcome.
editNote: Owner question: Does Oregon require franchise-document approval filing, and what must reach a buyer before a refundable deposit? Subtractive decision: Cut either “Replace registration none with a precise sales record” or “Worked example: an IT-services operator enters the plan”; neither needs a second full telling. Reduce the “useful management question” phrasing and final checklist to the specific delivery/proceeds facts not already stated. Final focus: Give the filing answer and deposit consequence directly, then briefly state records and separately linked existing-operator exceptions. Do not make correcting an internal worksheet the lesson.

learningSummary: Wisconsin describes registration as effective on receipt without merit review, but the buyer’s fourteen-calendar-day delivery period remains separate. Each franchise system needs its own filing.

sections.heading: Receipt does not replace earlier buyer delivery
paragraphs: The Department of Financial Institutions (DFI) says registration is required no later than the first Wisconsin franchise sale and is effective on receipt. It does not evaluate the opportunity’s merits.

Separately, give the Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD) fourteen calendar days before the earlier binding franchise or other agreement or payment. A same-day registration receipt does not show that a buyer received the correct package two weeks earlier.

sections.heading: An amendment does not restart the registration year
paragraphs: DFI lists $400 registration and one-year effectiveness, with separate filing for each system. Two service systems in one group therefore need their respective filings.

The agency lists material-event amendments within 30 days and $200. A corporate reorganization needs assessment as the actual possible event; waiting for annual renewal is not the stated amendment process. An amendment does not reset the year. Recheck current fees before payment.

sections.heading: Operating protections have an independent test
paragraphs: Chapter 135’s dealership/community-of-interest inquiry is separate from registration and federal fee analysis. The linked Fair Dealership Law guide explains cause, notice/cure and marked inventory, including why ten-day nonpayment cure is not automatic day-11 termination.

practicalOutput: Keep each system registered and deliver the correct buyer package early enough; address material events without waiting for renewal.
limitations: Actual system scope, offers and exemptions need application. Registration does not decide Fair Dealership Law coverage or approve the transaction.
editNote: Owner question: When must each Wisconsin franchise system be registered, and when must its buyer receive the FDD? Subtractive decision: Merge “Keep a separate event row for each franchise system” with the first two sections, keeping the deadlines and fees once. Shorten “Worked example: two service systems and a reorganisation”; replace the detailed “The operating relationship has its own legal test” discussion with the existing dealership-guide pointer. Final focus: Answer what must be complete for each system’s first sale and what a later amendment changes. Keep dealership exit rules on their existing dedicated page.

learningSummary: North Dakota removed the state-specific FDD addendum requirement from April 1, 2026. It did not remove registration, disclosure, amendments or actual financial-review conditions.

sections.heading: A submitted application is not enough
paragraphs: Section 51-19-02 combines the stated marketing plan/system, commercial symbol and direct/indirect fee, including area franchises. Required goods/services can matter; the wholesale-goods exclusion requires reasonable quantities. State-connected offers/acceptances and uninterrupted contract renewals/extensions also have defined treatment.
Section 51-19-03 requires registration or exemption before covered offer/sale. Under .07, filing, entry into the Commissioner’s register and absence of a stop order matter to effectiveness.

Material changes require prompt written amendment notification; approved amendments take effect on the Commissioner’s date. Conditional escrow/impoundment or a surety alternative depends on the statute and actual order.

sections.heading: Renewal still has an advance deadline
paragraphs: The agency directs renewal no later than fifteen business days before expiry unless the Commissioner waives the period. It describes twelve months unless an order/rule provides otherwise; use actual effective and expiry dates.

The April 1, 2026 notice removed one state-specific Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD) addendum. A contract-renewal exclusion does not remove registration renewal, and the addendum change does not remove financial review, disclosure or amendments.

sections.heading: Buyer delivery and anti-waiver remain
paragraphs: Section 51-19-08(6) has the stated seven-day prospectus/agreement delivery before the earlier agreement or consideration, signed receipt and three-year receipt retention. The independent federal fourteen-calendar-day rule is not shortened.
Section 51-19-16(7) voids purported waiver of compliance with the chapter, rules or orders. That is not a complete answer about all termination, renewal or specialized industry rights.

practicalOutput: Remove only the discontinued addendum from the process; confirm actual effectiveness, renewal and buyer-delivery requirements before offering or taking commitments.
limitations: Actual exemptions, state connections and orders require application. The addendum notice is not general deregulation, and the named anti-waiver rule is not a complete relationship-law review.
editNote: Owner question: Did removing the state addendum also remove renewal, and when is our renewal due? Subtractive decision: Cut the row “Can the buyer receive only the revised checklist?” and merge “Update only the checklist item the notice actually changed” with the renewal section. Remove the coordinator’s documented-checklist-revision narration from “Worked example: updating last year’s checklist”; keep the dated addendum change and actual renewal deadline directly. Final focus: Lead with the old requirement that disappeared and the obligations that still apply, then tell the seller which actual expiry/waiver facts govern renewal.

learningSummary: Rhode Island registration and exemption-notice periods start from different events. Registration relief also does not automatically remove buyer disclosure or prompt amendment duties.

sections.heading: Use the state definition and connections
paragraphs: Section 19-28.1-3 uses the stated marketing-plan/brand/fee-in-excess-of-$500 test and a separate master-franchise alternative. The wholesale exclusion concerns reasonable quantities of tangible goods; do not substitute a different federal amount.

Section 4 examines offer/acceptance connections, including an outside sale to a resident whose franchise will operate in Rhode Island. Residence, operation and communication/acceptance facts matter beyond the outlet address.

sections.heading: Use the actual starting event
paragraphs: Section 19-28.1-5 requires registration or exemption before covered offers/sales. Active rule 230-RICR-50-10-1.4 prescribes these periods; section 9(d)’s fiscal-year default yields to a director-prescribed rule or order.

rows: The statute calls for filing 30 days before actual expiration; apply the active period and any relevant order.

sections.heading: Check the separate relief from delivery
paragraphs: Section 8 requires disclosure reflecting all material changes and all proposed agreements at least fourteen calendar days before execution/payment, subject to listed exemption subsections.

A fractional franchise adds branded activity to an existing business. Rule 1.5’s qualified fractional route exempts registration and delivery with state-specific filing language and conditions concerning experience, location, similarity, expected revenue share and control. A federal fractional exemption does not establish it.
Section 11 requires prompt material-change amendments; the annual date is not permission to wait.

practicalOutput: Identify the exact registration or exemption period and any separate delivery relief before scheduling renewal or a buyer commitment.
limitations: Actual state connections, exemption conditions and orders require application. No universal fractional exemption or complete operating-law review is established.
editNote: Owner question: Does our annual period run from registration effectiveness or from receipt of an exemption notice? Subtractive decision: Keep one version of “Registration and an exemption notice have different anniversaries” and “Which date belongs in the Rhode Island anniversary field?” Move the fractional-route discussion and “Worked example: adding a branded technical service” out of the main date answer; reduce the filing-log instructions. Final focus: Answer the applicable start event, period and renewal lead using the existing route, rather than turning a date question into an incomplete exemption-selection lesson.

learningSummary: South Dakota’s notice filing, buyer delivery and financial-event reporting have different triggers. A complete notice may take effect on receipt, but that receipt does not start or replace the buyer’s disclosure period.

sections.heading: Complete notice receipt and annual renewal
paragraphs: SDCL 37-5B-4 requires a covered offer/sale to be properly notice filed or exempt. Section 5’s package contains the Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD), application, consent to service and $250 initial fee.

Effectiveness is generally on actual receipt, subject to completeness and stated order/injunction provisions. The usual period is one year from receipt unless another period is prescribed; renewal is $150 and late filings are treated as initial filings. Mailing is not receipt.

sections.heading: Apply each buyer-delivery condition
paragraphs: Use actual exemptions, versions and changed signing terms, not one generic waiting period.

rows: The stated seven-day branch. Prospect-initiated negotiation language in 17(2) does not erase section 26(7)’s separate materially-different-signing-terms rule.
Mail at least three days before the required delivery date; separate delivery/access instructions have their own treatment.
Obtain the prospect-signed receipt first and retain it three years.

sections.heading: No routine update filing does not mean no updating
paragraphs: Section 7 requires the revised annual disclosure within 120 days of fiscal close and reasonable-time quarterly material-change revisions, with prospects receiving the most recent available quarterly revisions, but no ordinary division filing for that updating. Known financial-performance changes have a separate notice duty.

Director-required amendments under section 6 and annual notice renewal remain distinct. After effectiveness, notice is required within fifteen days after the auditor reaches the specified going-concern conclusion about the business’s ability to continue. Apply any actual financial-assurance condition separately.

sections.heading: Advertising must remain supported
paragraphs: Section 37-5B-23 says ads need not be filed unless the director requests them, while allowing action against misleading advertising. That limited filing answer does not authorize unsupported revenue/profit claims.

practicalOutput: Use the actual notice receipt, delivery and auditor-conclusion events to meet their separate duties before relying on the offering or taking commitments.
limitations: Actual exemptions, orders, financial conditions and document changes require application. Notice receipt does not certify claims or approve a sale.
editNote: Owner question: What can affect a planned South Dakota signing, and what updates or audit events require action between renewals? Subtractive decision: Use “Sort each date by the event that starts it” as the main account and cut the repeated clock recital from the first three sections. Remove generic departmental narration in “Worked example: an audit issue during recruitment” and the table introduction; replace the double-negative update heading with the direct duty it explains. Final focus: Organise around the seller’s live decisions—whether the planned signing package is ready and whether a new financial or document event requires action—rather than the value of maintaining a calendar.

learningSummary: The New York Attorney General’s guide requires two copies of covered franchise advertising through NASAA FRED at least seven days before intended use. Submission does not certify the advertisement’s claims.

sections.heading: Submit the material you actually intend to use
paragraphs: FRED is the franchise filing system of the North American Securities Administrators Association. Identify the actual message, channel, sponsor and first-use date for the stated submission.

If a landing page changes after a PDF was submitted, compare the actual change and version with the submitted material before publication. A screenshot/version record is an optional business control, not a new legal filing category or a finding that every edit requires a new filing.

This page does not classify every website, message or conversation as a franchise advertisement. That decision depends on the actual communication; a format alone does not settle it. Registration, exemptions and buyer disclosure remain separate.

practicalOutput: Check whether the communication is covered and submit the actual intended advertising version on the required timetable.
limitations: Limited to the agency’s stated advertising submission rule. Classification of a particular communication and other pre-sale duties are not determined.
editNote: Owner question: What must we submit, and when, before using a covered New York franchise advertisement? Subtractive decision: Consolidation candidate with /states/new-york/ under “New information and new advertising need their own checks”; general campaign controls can sit with /us-expansion/advertising-controls/. Cut “Why marketing and sales need the same record,” the duplicate “Which version supports the scheduled landing page?” table and the worked example’s “That is an operational benefit” paragraph. Final focus: Provide the submission answer once in the state sales guide. A separate article needs a genuinely different, supported advertising question rather than more recordkeeping narration.
