learningSummary: Nebraska’s qualifying franchise exemption can still require a $100 notice before specified recruitment activity. If that exemption is not established, the nonexempt seller-assisted marketing plan route has different filing and buyer-delivery duties.

sections.heading: The qualifying franchise route
paragraphs: Section 59-1722’s conditional exemption from the Seller-Assisted Marketing Plans (SAMP) Act incorporates specified federal provisions as they existed January 1, 2026. A completed disclosure document or licence label alone does not establish those conditions.

The statute requires notice and a $100 fee before specified Nebraska-based advertising, offers or representations to Nebraska prospects. The notice identifies the actual seller, contacts, operating name and plan. Some prohibitions remain despite exemption.

The regulator describes this as a one-time notice without renewal, distinguishing contact-only amendments from other changes. One time does not mean every later change is irrelevant. Acknowledgement is not approval or verification of profit claims.

sections.heading: The covered nonexempt route is different
paragraphs: Section 59-1724 requires prior disclosure filing and $100 fee, material-change filings and annual updates for a covered nonexempt SAMP.

Section 59-1732 addresses disclosure at the first specified in-person or written communication and at least 48 hours before the relevant contract or consideration. These duties do not shorten independently applicable federal disclosure.

practicalOutput: Choose the actual route before the recruitment campaign, using the seller, message and Nebraska connections rather than signing day alone.
limitations: Limited to the stated filing and disclosure branches, not every Nebraska sales, relationship or operating duty.
editNote: Owner question: Does a qualifying franchise exemption let us recruit Nebraska prospects without a prior state notice? Subtractive decision: Keep the two route descriptions or “Choose one route for the training campaign before scheduling it,” not both. Cut the worked example’s second paragraph beginning “The reviewer establishes whether…” because it simply repeats the conditional routes without explaining their selection; reduce the decision-sheet checklist. Final focus: Answer what the qualifying exemption removes, what prior notice it retains and how that differs from the nonexempt route, before explaining record retention.

learningSummary: Nevada’s named farm-equipment dealer law can govern exit or major contract changes, but the 180-day notice is not a universal amendment rule. Establish its defined dealer relationship first.

sections.heading: This is not every service or equipment business
paragraphs: NRS 597.112–.118 concerns defined farm-equipment arrangements, including retail inventory rights, a distribution-system role and substantial supplier dependence. Inventory means the defined equipment, attachments or repair parts. A service brand or software licence does not qualify just because the contract says dealer.

sections.heading: Match the action to its conditions
paragraphs: Section 597.1143 generally requires good cause, 180 days’ written reasons before termination/nonrenewal and 60 days to correct specified deficiencies. Listed grounds have different treatment; market-share failure has an assistance condition. Waiting alone does not prove cause.
Subsection (1) also requires good cause for a substantial agreement change, but the 180/60 provisions in (2)–(3) concern termination/nonrenewal, not every amendment.

Section 597.115(4) separately addresses action because of natural disaster, labour dispute or similar circumstances beyond the dealer’s control. Section 597.118 prohibits waiver/modification of the statutory rights, obligations and liabilities.

sections.heading: Buyback needs item eligibility, not a stock total
paragraphs: Repurchase rules and exclusions depend on condition, age and other facts, including specified supplier-required systems/tools. Purchase and supplier-requirement records matter; gross stock or technology spending does not establish what must be repurchased.

practicalOutput: Identify coverage and whether the actual proposal is exit or substantial amendment before selecting notice or buyback assumptions.
limitations: Limited to defined farm-equipment dealers. Actual cause, exceptions and repurchase eligibility are not determined.
editNote: Owner question: Do we need the same process to change a farm dealer’s terms as to end or not renew the agreement? Subtractive decision: Cut “Choose the farm-machine action before copying a notice” if retaining the preceding detailed amendment/termination sections. Reduce the worked example to the actual amendment-versus-termination contrast; keep buyback as a short separate consequence rather than repeating its stock-record warning in the checklist. Final focus: Begin with the action the supplier intends to take and explain which parts of the exit process do and do not apply to a substantial amendment.

learningSummary: A New Hampshire master-operator plan needs examination of required investments and successive recruiting rights—not just its territory count. Real support duties do not automatically resolve the defined chain-distributor test.

sections.heading: Trace what each participant buys and may recruit
paragraphs: RSA 358-B addresses participants investing and receiving rights to recruit others for economic gain, with those participants also investing and receiving recruiting rights. A master-franchise label, recruitment fee alone or genuine support work alone does not establish every element.

For example, a regional partner paid when operators join, where operators may buy rights to recruit further operators, needs the actual investments, rights and compensation source traced through each level. Separating customer-service revenue from joining/recruitment payments is an optional way to expose those facts, not a safe harbour.

sections.heading: A cap does not change a prohibited structure
paragraphs: The law says participant limits or eligibility conditions do not themselves change the identity of the defined scheme. Offering only ten regional territories therefore does not answer the test.

Where the prohibited device is established, the chapter prohibits promotion, offering or granting participation. Review the actual structure before recruitment, without treating every master or multi-level arrangement as unlawful.

practicalOutput: Clarify required investments, successive recruiting rights and compensation before promoting participation.
limitations: Only RSA 358-B’s specified branch is reviewed. Franchise disclosure, consumer, dealer and operating requirements remain separate and are not assumed absent.
editNote: Owner question: Does limiting the network to ten territories avoid the chain-distributor prohibition? Subtractive decision: Merge “Follow the technical network’s payment through the levels” with “Worked example: a technical-services network”; retain one telling of the paid successive recruiting rights and ten-territory cap. Cut “A useful management exercise…” and repeated costed-support-plan instructions from the surrounding sections and closing checklist. Final focus: Answer the territory-cap misconception through the actual sequence of who pays and obtains further recruiting rights. Explain genuine customer/support activity only insofar as it does not replace the complete test.

learningSummary: A New Jersey office-based distributor can fall within the Franchise Practices Act, but office activity alone is not enough. Establish the written brand/community-of-interest relationship and the applicable combined criteria.

sections.heading: The Act has its own relationship definition
paragraphs: Section 56:10-3 requires the stated written arrangement for a definite or indefinite period, permission to use a trade name/mark/service mark or related characteristics, and a community of interest—the parties’ shared commercial interest—in marketing goods or services. A distribution label does not decide those facts.

For the place-of-business test, an office or warehouse is generally excluded. But for persons without a majority of sales directly to consumers, qualifying offices/warehouses from which personnel visit/call customers or goods are delivered can count. An address alone is insufficient.

sections.heading: For the general route, all three application criteria matter
paragraphs: Section 56:10-4(a) requires the following together for the franchisee, the operator receiving the rights. Section 4(b) has a separate new-motor-vehicle franchise route, not the same three-test rule.

rows: Performance contemplates or requires the franchisee to establish/maintain the defined location.
Covered product/service gross sales exceeded $35,000 during the twelve months immediately before suit is instituted.
More than 20% of the franchisee’s gross sales are intended to be or derived from the franchise.

sections.heading: Coverage is not a ruling on this operator
paragraphs: Section 56:10-8 excludes a franchise granted before the Act’s effective date, while renewal or amendment is not excluded on that basis. The source gives December 21, 1971 as the Act’s effective date.

The identified 2025 federal opinion considered pleaded allegations, not final factual findings about every distributor. Current definitions/application text is now readable, but this limited coverage guide does not supply the complete sector, case-law, filing, disclosure or exit analysis.

practicalOutput: Apply the actual relationship, location and sales facts to the correct route before relying on ongoing franchise protection.
limitations: Limited to the identified definitions, application criteria and prior-grant rule. Industry exceptions, complete case law and sales/exit procedures are not determined; the cited 2025 opinion tested allegations, not final facts.
editNote: Owner question: Can we dismiss franchise protection just because the operator sells to businesses from an office or warehouse? Subtractive decision: Keep one prominent current-codification gap note; cut the duplicate “Read these limited-source answers before using the example” table and repeated gap narration in “Keep the source limitation visible.” Shorten “Prepare the reviewer’s factual file” and remove the example’s speculative future-withdrawal paragraph. Final focus: Present a bounded explanation of the office/warehouse misconception and those particular sources, not a current eligibility, filing or exit guide. learningSummary: New Mexico SB 115 of 2026 did not enact the proposed equipment-dealer changes. Its precise notice language or proposed effective date cannot be used as the current exit rule.

sections.heading: The verified result is non-enactment
paragraphs: The official status records “Died (API)”, meaning action postponed indefinitely. The introduced text and analysis discussed expanded equipment definitions and termination protections, but those changes did not become law through this bill.

The Fiscal Impact Report also says similar 2023 and 2025 proposals were not enacted. A proposed effective date depends on enactment; neither introduced text nor analysis replaces an enacted chapter or the current statute.
Current Franchise Termination Act coverage and procedure were not established here. Failure of this bill does not show that existing dealer protections or franchise filing duties are absent.

practicalOutput: Do not use SB 115’s proposed terms in an exit decision; establish the actual current statute for the products and agreement.
limitations: The verified conclusion is the identified proposal’s non-enactment, not a current notice period or permission to terminate.
editNote: Owner question: Did 2026 SB 115 enact the dealer-termination changes described in that proposal? Subtractive decision: Condense the official “Died (API)” result and its precise limit into a New Mexico coverage/status note; the generic bill-versus-law lesson fits /methodology/. Cut the duplicate “Which document answers the machinery supplier’s question?” table, template-correction story and “Keep a source-status record alongside the contract” checklist. Final focus: Use a short dated legislative-status correction, with a direct statement that existing enacted coverage/notice remains unanswered. Do not present a failed-proposal lesson as operational New Mexico guidance.

learningSummary: A federally registered mark can answer North Carolina’s specified marketing-program branch without removing a separate income guarantee or buyback trigger. Test the actual promise before treating the offer as excluded.

sections.heading: A mark is only one branch
paragraphs: Article 19 describes specified device-placement help, buying purchaser-produced products, income/refund promises and sales/marketing programs. Section 66-94(4)’s mark exception requires the stated U.S. federal registration; a home registration or pending application is not equivalent.

Ordinary customer-location help is not automatically the specified vending or similar-device placement. Section 66-94.1’s separate responsible-seller exemption has actual conditions and a sworn filing; reputation alone is insufficient.

For an actual income or refund promise, check whether the relevant provision requires a bond or trust, a form of financial protection. This is a conditional question, not a bond requirement for every offer.

sections.heading: If covered, file before the campaign
paragraphs: Section 66-97 requires filing before advertisements or other representations to prospective purchasers in the state, material-change updates and updates at least annually.

sections.heading: The buyer period is a different duty
paragraphs: Section 66-95 requires covered disclosure at least 48 hours before the earlier signature or receipt of consideration (money or other relevant value). A materially compliant federal Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD) is one permitted content route.
Using an FDD does not shorten the independently applicable federal fourteen-calendar-day period. Filing with the state and delivering to the buyer are different events.

practicalOutput: Separate each promise and establish the exact exclusion or exemption before advertising; if covered, meet filing and buyer delivery independently.
limitations: Limited to the stated business-opportunity branches. Actual mark/responsible-seller conditions and other sales or relationship requirements are not determined.
editNote: Owner question: Does our registered U.S. mark remove business-opportunity duties when we also promise income or refunds? Subtractive decision: Remove the repeated sentence “The responsible-seller exemption also has its own conditions and sworn filing; reputation is not that filing.” Merge “Sort the Singapore offer before relying on its mark” with the cleaning-guarantee example; trim the closing sheet instructions already covered by filing and delivery sections. Final focus: Explain which actual promise survives the proposed mark-based reasoning and what that changes for the campaign or guarantee, rather than instructing the owner to maintain another factsheet.

learningSummary: Ohio’s materially FTC-compliant transaction exemption preserves named security and buyback provisions. A federal disclosure document is not the complete answer where the sales promise says the buyer’s payment is secured or a buyback exists.

sections.heading: The exemption leaves sections 1334.03(H) and 1334.04
paragraphs: Section 1334.13 removes most of the Business Opportunity Plans chapter for materially Federal Trade Commission (FTC)-compliant transactions, but expressly preserves these sections on payment/note security or buyback representations and related bond/trust duties.
Apply those surviving provisions to the actual equipment or protection promise; a compliant franchise disclosure package does not itself establish a bond or trust arrangement.

sections.heading: Ohio has its own definition and proof rules
paragraphs: Section 1334.01 uses supplied goods/services, payment conditions and specified representations. Its payment analysis is not the federal minimum-payment exemption.
Other exceptions appear in .12. In proceedings under .08 or .09, section .14 places the exemption/exception proof burden on the claimant.

sections.heading: The nonexempt buyer route is conditional
paragraphs: Covered nonexempt plans have disclosure, claim-substantiation, contract and cancellation provisions. The basic disclosure period is ten business days before agreement. The reviewed business-day definition excludes Sunday and legal holidays; a Monday–Friday calculator may be wrong.
Section 1334.05 cancellation is a separate conditional process, not a universal cancellation right for every franchise buyer. Independently applicable federal duties remain separate.

practicalOutput: Check any secured-payment or buyback promise against the surviving provisions even if the federal-compliance exemption otherwise applies.
limitations: The actual exemption, bond/trust and cancellation conditions are not decided. This is not complete Ohio franchise, dealer or operating coverage.
editNote: Owner question: If our franchise offer is materially FTC-compliant, do Ohio’s security and buyback rules still matter? Subtractive decision: Cut the added “Two self-checks” table or merge its first two rows into the “fully secured” example; it is not two checks as labelled. Keep the unusual business-day definition once with nonexempt timing, and remove the table’s repeated cancellation question plus generic “Assemble the exemption and promise file” narration. Final focus: Lead with what the security/buyback promise leaves the seller responsible for checking after the claimed exemption. Keep the nonexempt calendar as a secondary, clearly separate case.

learningSummary: Oklahoma’s disclosure-based exemption removes sections 806–811, not the whole Act. Actual delivery fourteen calendar days before the earlier commitment is a condition; preparing a document is not delivery.

sections.heading: Establish the particular exemption and state connections
paragraphs: The Act prohibits covered offers/sales without registration or exemption. Section 803(6) provides the stated business-opportunity/franchise route when the specified document is delivered fourteen calendar days before the earlier binding agreement or consideration (money or other value).

Section 802 has its own business-opportunity, franchise and marketing-plan definitions, including relevant account-finding/training promises. The registered-mark/net-worth exclusion has further conditions. Section 805 puts proof of exemption/exclusion/exception on its claimant.

Section 818 separately examines offer origin/receipt, acceptance, domicile (the legally relevant home connection) and operating location. An outside outlet or internet format does not establish a blanket result for discovery calls or campaigns.

sections.heading: Registration effectiveness and advertising remain distinct
paragraphs: Section 807 describes complete filing, effectiveness normally after fifteen full business days absent stated orders/proceedings, and one-year duration. An incomplete upload does not automatically become effective.

Sections 819–822 address fraud and misleading claims, including representing a filing as approval. The current administrative advertising-filing text could not be confirmed after agency-site failure; absence of a retrieved rule is not evidence of no advertising duty.

practicalOutput: Establish the exact exemption or complete registration route and resolve the current advertising rule before relying on a campaign timetable.
limitations: Actual definition, state connections and exemptions need application. The administrative advertising-filing rule remains unresolved.
editNote: Owner question: What is the difference between the stated fourteen-day disclosure exemption and the registration process? Subtractive decision: Remove the “all three routes” framing and merge the added table into the two actual statutory-route explanations. Keep the unconfirmed advertising rule in one prominent scope note, not the title’s promised answer plus repeated table/paragraph/checklist entries; shorten the Dutch campaign’s manager-by-manager fact collection. Final focus: Answer the limited statutory comparison honestly and identify advertising as a separate unresolved question, not as a third completed option or a campaign-clearance lesson.

learningSummary: Pennsylvania’s named vehicle-dealer repurchase provision has two clocks: return generally within 90 days of the relevant end event, and repurchase/payment within 60 days of tender. Tender means the legally relevant offer of covered property for return; its date is not necessarily the physical return date. The two clocks have different triggers.

sections.heading: Section 316 is not a general franchise refund
paragraphs: The Board of Vehicles Act defines the dealer/franchise relationship and eligible inventory/equipment after specified termination or nonrenewal. Product category, condition, acquisition age and other limits matter, including particular treatment of motorcycle, recreational-vehicle and manufactured-housing arrangements.

A stock ledger or total startup spending does not establish eligibility. Vehicle identity/date/mileage/condition, parts, required tools/signs and ownership or creditor interests can matter to the actual item review; keeping those details is preparation, not expanded statutory coverage.

sections.heading: Separate the return event from tender
paragraphs: Apply section 316’s actual eligible-property and event conditions before calculating a deadline.

practicalOutput: Establish the eligible property and actual termination/nonrenewal and tender dates before claiming a return or payment deadline.
limitations: Limited to the named vehicle-dealer branch. Actual item conditions, category exceptions and repurchase entitlement are not decided, and this is not a service-franchise exit formula.
editNote: Owner question: Does the buyback payment deadline run from the dealer agreement’s end, return of stock or tender? Subtractive decision: Keep one account of “There are two events and two clocks” and the first two rows of “Two starting events, not one exit countdown.” Cut “Keep commercial planning distinct from legal entitlement”; shorten the specialist-manufacturer story and final exit-file list, which repeat the item-record instructions. Final focus: Explain the act that starts each deadline and why the same exit date cannot automatically be used for both. Keep only evidence that determines eligibility or proves tender/return.

learningSummary: South Carolina examines the actual startup promises, not only the brand’s registration. A refund or earnings promise can raise a different definition branch from the marketing program.

sections.heading: The mark exception is limited
paragraphs: Section 39-57-20 has specified business-startup arrangements and representations. The registered-mark exception sits within its sales/marketing-program branch; device-placement assistance, purchasing buyer-made products and guarantee/refund promises have their own terms.

Apply the fee condition and other exclusions too. Ordinary customer-finding is not automatically vending-device placement. A cleaning support offer with a startup refund needs that actual refund promise tested separately, including unresolved financial-protection conditions.

sections.heading: Covered promotion needs filing and claims support
paragraphs: Section 39-57-50 requires filing before advertisements or other representations, use of the assigned registration number in promotion, material-change updates and updates at least biennially (once every two years). A filing number is not endorsement; statements about state compliance have separate limits.
Section 39-57-60(1) requires documented evidence supporting the earnings claim to be disclosed when the representation is made. Internal possession of a spreadsheet is not that disclosure.

Section 39-57-30 separately requires disclosure 48 hours before the earlier business-opportunity contract or consideration (money or other value). Independently applicable federal disclosure is not shortened.

practicalOutput: Separate the actual marketing, refund and income promises before promotion; if covered, complete filing and provide the required claim evidence and buyer disclosure.
limitations: Limited to the stated business-opportunity branches. Actual fees, representations, exclusions and financial-protection conditions are not determined.
editNote: Owner question: Does our mark or refund promise change what we must file or tell a buyer before selling the package? Subtractive decision: Keep either “Match the promise to its own provision” or the duplicated rule paragraphs as the primary account. learningSummary: Tennessee franchise tax and selling a franchise are different subjects. The cited Revenue FAQs identify entity-tax questions; they do not establish permission to recruit a branded operator.

sections.heading: Federal disregarded status does not finish state tax
paragraphs: Revenue’s F&E-1 FAQ lists corporations, limited liability companies (LLCs) and other entity types that may have return obligations. F&E-4 explains that a federally disregarded LLC—ignored as a separate entity for the relevant federal tax purpose—can still need a Tennessee return unless an exemption applies.

These FAQs are dated March 2021. The actual taxpayer, federal classification, Tennessee activities/connections, tax year, current law and exemption conditions still need examination. They are not a complete current calculation or filing calendar.

A Singapore parent, U.S. LLC and Tennessee operator can therefore have different factual roles. Completing the LLC’s tax account does not resolve the separate brand-rights, fee, control and support arrangement.

sections.heading: Current franchise-sales rules remain unresolved
paragraphs: The June 2021 consumer-agency help explanation identifies its consumer-protection role, not current franchise statutory requirements. Attempts to retrieve the linked code and court text did not provide usable legal bodies.
State offer/sale filings, exemptions, advertising and relationship rules are not established here. Failed access is not proof of no duty; independently applicable federal disclosure remains separate.

practicalOutput: Identify the actual taxpayer and current tax-year questions without treating a tax account as permission to sell franchise rights.
limitations: Limited to the tax-versus-sales distinction from dated FAQs. Current tax scope and Tennessee franchise-law coverage remain unresolved.

learningSummary: On Utah’s qualifying franchise route, proof of the issued notice receipt must precede the covered offer or sale. A prepared notice or completed disclosure document is not that receipt.

sections.heading: The trigger includes Utah residents
paragraphs: Section 13-15-201(2) addresses a franchise to be located in Utah or offered/sold to a Utah resident. An out-of-state outlet does not remove the resident branch.

The notice states substantial federal Franchise Rule compliance and includes the required applicant, brand, address and public identification information. The actual seller and qualifying conditions still matter.

sections.heading: Three dates under the section effective May 6, 2026

rows: Valid for one year from issue.
Compliance at least 30 days before expiry.
Update within 30 days of that event, not just at annual renewal.

sections.heading: The general business-opportunity route differs
paragraphs: Section 201(2)(c) directs those not qualifying for the franchise notice to subsection (1), with its own disclosure content and ten-business-day purchaser-delivery provisions.
Neither receipt is state approval. Independently applicable federal FDD (Franchise Disclosure Document) delivery remains separate from the Utah receipt.

practicalOutput: Establish the qualifying route and obtain proof of notice receipt before the covered offer; use issue and information-change dates for their separate duties.
limitations: Actual seller, resident/location facts and compliance conditions are not determined. This does not complete every filing, disclosure or operating requirement.

learningSummary: Vermont’s equipment-dealer exit rules depend on the defined products and the reason for ending the arrangement. A general 120-day notice is not the process for every event.

sections.heading: Check products and dealer status
paragraphs: Title 9, Chapter 107 has dealer and inventory definitions and can cover oral/written agreements. Heavy construction equipment and a specified single-line category are excluded.
Adding utility-equipment sales/repairs to a service offer raises a different question from the brand licence alone. Describe the actual equipment relationship before selecting an exit branch.

sections.heading: Use the process for the actual ground
paragraphs: Section 4072 generally requires cause, 120 days’ notice and a 60-day opportunity to correct the stated problem. Market-penetration termination has a separate initial 24-month period and final-notice process. Specified events allow immediate termination. The special market-penetration and immediate-event procedures are not fully set out here.
An alleged performance problem does not establish cause or a listed immediate event. Do not substitute the general period for the actual market-penetration requirements.

sections.heading: Stock value is not a repurchase claim
paragraphs: Sections 4073–4074 make repurchase subject to request, item eligibility, valuation and payment requirements. Source, age, condition, title and the actual request matter; the total inventory account is not an automatic reimbursement.

practicalOutput: Confirm coverage and the actual exit ground, then apply its notice/correction process and item-specific repurchase conditions separately.
limitations: Limited to the named equipment-dealer branch. Actual exclusions, cause, immediate-event and repurchase conditions are not determined.

learningSummary: West Virginia’s Farm Equipment Dealer Contract Act can include specified construction, industrial and outdoor-power sellers. If covered, its six-month notice is a prescribed procedure—not an assumed number of days or an informal email.

sections.heading: Check retail sales, inventory and repairs
paragraphs: Coverage includes the stated retail sellers and inventory/repair-service conditions. A service licence alone does not establish it, and industrial rather than farm use does not automatically exclude it.

sections.heading: Apply the stated service, contents and exception conditions
paragraphs: Section 47-11F-3 generally requires six months’ termination notice, prescribed written service and contents. Listed exceptions and the mutual-consent route need separate application.
A contract clause or ordinary message does not establish the statutory procedure. Keep the period as six months rather than converting it to a fixed day count.

sections.heading: Value, return and payment are different questions
paragraphs: Sections 4–5 govern conditional inventory repurchase, including valuation, timing and exclusions. Source, age, condition, title and current-net-price evidence matter; a retail price or gross stock balance is not automatically the statutory value.
Track actual termination, physical return and payment separately, including responsible payer and unresolved warranty questions. Budgeting possible exposure does not establish entitlement.

practicalOutput: Establish dealer coverage, then apply the actual notice procedure and item-specific return/payment conditions.
limitations: Limited to the named equipment branch. Definitions, notice exceptions, mutual-consent and repurchase conditions are not determined for an actual arrangement.

learningSummary: Wyoming’s ordinary equipment-dealer notice differs for the general and single-line branches. You must establish the actual category before choosing 180 or 90 days; neither is automatic exit permission. This page compares the ordinary tracks; it does not supply the full single-line eligibility or special-event/performance tests.

sections.heading: Start with equipment and granted rights
paragraphs: Chapter 40-20 covers defined equipment dealers/suppliers, including specified industrial, maintenance, utility and grounds-care equipment. Actual products, sale/repair rights, agreement, exclusions and single-line conditions matter; using equipment or one brand does not itself settle them.

sections.heading: The two ordinary tracks
paragraphs: Specified events and performance failures have different conditions; actual reasons, comparable standards and improvement history remain necessary.

rows: 180 days’ notice, sixty days to cure.
Ninety days’ notice, sixty days to cure.

sections.heading: Notice does not decide buyback or succession
paragraphs: Sections 120–121 have separate repurchase duties/exclusions. Actual property source, dates, condition, return and payment conditions determine item treatment; not every startup cost is recoverable.
Use the inventory companion for those details. Any succession request also needs its actual facts rather than an answer copied from the termination calendar.

practicalOutput: Establish the actual dealer category and proposed action before selecting the notice branch; assess inventory and succession independently.
limitations: Limited to the defined equipment branch, not a general Wyoming franchise exit rule. Actual performance, exception and category conditions remain necessary.
